P.n: Sapporo Clock Tower (札幌市時計台)
P.ad: Kita 1-jo Nishi 2-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0001, Japan
P.w: The 1878 wooden drill hall of the Sapporo Agricultural College, its clock still striking the hours — the city's symbol and an Important Cultural Property.

P.n: Former Hokkaido Government Office (Akarenga, 赤れんが庁舎)
P.ad: Kita 3-jo Nishi 6-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-8588, Japan
P.w: The 1888 neo-baroque red-brick seat of the Hokkaido Development Commission — reopened 25 July 2025 after a multi-year restoration as a museum of Hokkaido history with a free garden.

P.n: Ōdōri Park (大通公園)
P.ad: Ōdōri Nishi 1–12-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0042, Japan
P.w: The 1.5 km green firebreak that splits Sapporo north from south — stage of the Sapporo Snow Festival in February, beer gardens and the autumn food festival.

P.n: Moerenuma Park (モエレ沼公園)
P.w: Isamu Noguchi's last great work: a former landfill sculpted into one park-sized artwork — Mt Moere, the Glass Pyramid, the Sea Fountain.

P.n: Historical Village of Hokkaido (北海道開拓の村)
P.ad: 50-1 Konopporo, Atsubetsu-chō, Atsubetsu-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 004-0006, Japan
P.w: Open-air museum of 50-plus relocated Meiji–early Shōwa buildings — herring lodges, farmhouses, a horse-drawn tram — telling the story of Hokkaido's settlement.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — Noda Satoru's building reference; filming location of the 2024 live-action film (Sugimoto's horse-sleigh drag on the main street) · open-air museum meiji

P.n: Sapporo Hitsujigaoka Observation Hill (さっぽろ羊ヶ丘展望台)
P.w: The hill with the bronze of Dr William S. Clark pointing to the horizon ('Boys, be ambitious!') over sheep pasture and the Ishikari Plain.

P.n: Mount Moiwa (藻岩山)
P.w: Ropeway and mini-cable car to a 531 m summit for one of Japan's 'new three great night views' over the Sapporo grid.

P.n: Hokkaido Shrine (北海道神宮)
P.w: Hokkaido's principal Shinto shrine in the Maruyama primeval forest, founded 1869 for the island's pioneer deities — cherry and plum blossom in spring.

P.n: Sapporo TV Tower (さっぽろテレビ塔)
P.ad: Ōdōri Nishi 1-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0042, Japan
P.w: The 147 m 1957 tower at the head of Ōdōri Park — the 90 m deck looks straight down the park's length.

P.n: Sapporo Beer Museum (サッポロビール博物館)
P.ad: Kita 7-jo Higashi 9-chome 1-1, Higashi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 065-8633, Japan
P.w: Japan's only beer museum, in the 1890 red-brick Sapporo Sugar Company building — the story of the oldest Japanese beer brand, with a tasting salon.

P.n: Hokkaido University Botanic Garden (北海道大学植物園)
P.ad: Kita 3-jo Nishi 8-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0003, Japan
P.w: A 13 ha 1886 garden in the middle of downtown — native Hokkaido flora, Ainu ethnographic collection and the Miyabe memorial.

P.n: Jōzankei Onsen (定山渓温泉)
P.ad: Jōzankei Onsen, Minami-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 061-2302, Japan
P.w: Sapporo's own hot-spring town an hour south, in a Toyohira River gorge inside Shikotsu-Tōya National Park — foot baths and autumn colour.

P.n: Otaru Canal (小樽運河)
P.w: The 1923 freight canal lined with stone warehouses and gas lamps — Otaru's postcard, best at dusk and during the February Snow Light Path.

P.n: Sakaimachi Street (堺町通り)
P.w: The preserved Meiji–Taishō merchant street a short walk from the canal — glass workshops, music boxes, LeTAO and Kitakaro sweet shops.

P.n: Otaru Music Box Museum (小樽オルゴール堂)
P.w: The 1912 brick main hall at the foot of Sakaimachi, packed with thousands of music boxes — the Vancouver-gifted steam clock whistles out front. Free entry.

P.n: Nikka Whisky Yoichi Distillery (ニッカウヰスキー余市蒸溜所)
P.ad: Kurokawa-chō, Yoichi, Yoichi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Masataka Taketsuru's 1934 distillery, chosen because Yoichi most resembled Scotland — coal-fired pot stills, stone kilns and a tasting hall.

P.n: Otaru City General Museum (小樽市総合博物館)
P.w: Hokkaido's railway birthplace — steam locomotives in the old Temiya roundhouse, plus the canal-side annex in a former warehouse.

P.n: Goryōkaku (五稜郭)
P.w: Japan's first Western-style fortress, the 1866 star fort where the Republic of Ezo made its last stand — a thousand cherry trees fill the moats in spring.

P.n: Mount Hakodate (函館山)
P.w: 334 m peak at the tip of the peninsula: a three-minute ropeway to one of Japan's great night views, the city lights pinched between two bays.

P.n: Motomachi (元町)
P.w: The slope-side former foreign settlement — churches, the Old British Consulate, the Chinese Memorial Hall and the Old Public Hall of Hakodate Ward on stepped streets down to the harbour.

P.n: Hakodate Orthodox Church (Holy Resurrection, ハリストス正教会)
P.w: Japan's first Orthodox parish (consecrated 1860); the 1916 white church with green copper domes is an Important Cultural Property.

P.n: Hakodate Morning Market (函館朝市)
P.w: 250-odd stalls across the street from Hakodate Station — squid you fish yourself, crab, uni and ikura donburi for breakfast.

P.n: Matsumae Castle (松前城)
P.ad: Matsushiro, Matsumae, Matsumae District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's northernmost castle, seat of the only Edo-period domain on Hokkaido — its park is one of the island's great cherry-blossom spots, thousands of trees in 250 varieties.

P.n: Upopoy — National Ainu Museum & Park (ウポポイ)
P.ad: Wakakusa-chō, Shiraoi, Shiraoi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's national centre for Ainu culture on Lake Poroto — the museum, a kotan of chise houses, dance, music and Ainu cooking.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — partner of the official 'Golden Kamuy × Hokkaido' campaign; the National Ainu Museum held a Golden Kamuy special exhibition · ainu museum

P.n: Noboribetsu Jigokudani (登別地獄谷)
P.w: 'Hell Valley' above Hokkaido's most famous onsen town — a steaming crater of sulphur vents feeding nine kinds of spring water, boardwalk to Oyunuma.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — Noboribetsu Onsen is the 7th Division's convalescent spa in the story; 2024 Hell Festival collaboration · hell valley onsen

P.n: Lake Tōya (洞爺湖)
P.ad: Tōyako Onsen, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Round caldera lake with an island at its heart and Mount Usu steaming on its shore — onsen town, summer fireworks every night.

P.n: Mount Usu (有珠山)
P.w: Active volcano that last erupted in 2000 — the Usuzan Ropeway rises to crater rims and views over Lake Tōya and Shōwa-shinzan.

P.n: Lake Shikotsu (支笏湖)
P.w: Japan's northernmost ice-free lake and one of its deepest and clearest — a caldera ringed by volcanoes an hour from Sapporo.

P.n: Asahiyama Zoo (旭山動物園)
P.w: The zoo that reinvented Japanese zoos with behavioural exhibits — penguin parade in the snow, polar bears and seals in see-through tubes.

P.n: Blue Pond, Biei (青い池)
P.ad: Shirogane, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: An accidental pond behind a volcanic-mudflow dam whose aluminium-rich water turns an unreal cobalt around drowned larches.

P.n: Sōunkyō Gorge (層雲峡)
P.ad: Sōunkyō, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Onsen town in a 100 m-cliffed gorge of the Ishikari River — Ginga and Ryūsei falls, and the Kurodake ropeway into Daisetsuzan.

P.n: Mount Asahidake (旭岳)
P.ad: Asahidake Onsen, Higashikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's highest peak (2,291 m) in Daisetsuzan National Park — a ropeway to steaming fumaroles and alpine tundra, Japan's first autumn colour.

P.n: Shiretoko Five Lakes (知床五湖)
P.ad: Onnebetsu, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Five forest lakes under the Shiretoko range inside the UNESCO World Natural Heritage site — an 800 m bear-proof elevated boardwalk plus guided ground trails.

P.n: Furepe Waterfall (フレペの滝)
P.ad: Iwaobetsu, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 'The Maiden's Tears' — groundwater seeping straight out of a sea cliff into the Sea of Okhotsk, twenty minutes' walk from the Shiretoko Nature Center.

P.n: Oshinkoshin Falls (オシンコシンの滝)
P.ad: Chashikotsu, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Twin-stream roadside falls on the way to Utoro, one of Japan's 100 best waterfalls, with a stair up to the mid-fall viewpoint.

P.n: Shiretoko Pass (知床峠)
P.ad: Shiretoko-tōge, between Utoro (Shari) and Rausu, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 738 m road pass across the peninsula, facing Mount Rausu and, across the strait, Kunashiri Island; open roughly May to early November.

P.n: Lake Mashū (摩周湖)
P.w: The Ainu 'Lake of the Gods': a 212 m-deep caldera with no inlet or outlet, famous for 'Mashū blue' clarity — and its fogs.

P.n: Lake Akan (阿寒湖)
P.ad: Akanko Onsen, Akan-chō, Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Crater lake under Me-Akan and O-Akan, home of the spherical marimo algae, with the Akankohan onsen town on its shore.

P.n: Lake Kussharo (屈斜路湖)
P.w: Japan's largest caldera lake — hot sand you dig into at Sunayu, open-air shore baths and winter swans.

P.n: Mount Iō — Iōzan (硫黄山 / Atosanupuri)
P.ad: Kawayu Onsen, Teshikaga, Kawakami District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The Ainu 'naked mountain': a bare, yellow-crusted active volcano hissing sulphur steam beside Kawayu Onsen.

P.n: Abashiri Prison Museum (博物館 網走監獄)
P.w: The Meiji prison that built Hokkaido's roads, rebuilt as an open-air museum — the five-winged radial cell block, court, bathhouse and punishment cells.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — Abashiri Prison is a central setting of the manga/anime, drawing a wave of younger visitors · prison museum

P.n: Kushiro Marsh — Kushiro-shitsugen National Park (釧路湿原)
P.ad: Hosooka Observatory (細岡展望台), Kushiro-chō, Kushiro District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's largest wetland and first Ramsar site (1980) — the stronghold of the red-crowned crane, seen from the Hosooka and marsh observatories.

P.n: Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses (金森赤レンガ倉庫)
P.w: 1909 harbour warehouses (founded 1887) turned shops, beer hall and event space in 1988 — Hakodate's waterfront landmark.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Love Live! Sunshine!! — Hakodate pilgrimage stop from the S2 Hakodate arc · red brick warehouse bay

P.n: Ōnuma Quasi-National Park (大沼国定公園)
P.ad: Ōnuma-chō, Nanae, Kameda District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Island-dotted Ōnuma and Konuma ponds under the volcano Hokkaidō-Komagatake — 126 islets linked by bridges, boating and cycling 30 minutes from Hakodate.

P.n: Cape Sōya (宗谷岬)
P.w: The northernmost point you can stand on in Japan — the triangular monument, Sakhalin on the horizon on a clear day.

P.n: Rishiri Island & Mount Rishiri (利尻島・利尻山)
P.ad: Rishiri / Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A dormant 1,721 m volcano rising straight from the sea — 'Rishiri-Fuji' — ringed by a cycling road and kelp-drying beaches; ferry from Wakkanai.

P.n: Rebun Island (礼文島)
P.w: The 'floating island of flowers' — alpine flowers found nowhere else bloom at sea level June–August along the Momoiwa and Cape Sukoton trails.

P.n: Taushubetsu River Bridge (タウシュベツ川橋梁)
P.ad: Nukabira, Kamishihoro, Katō District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1937 concrete arch viaduct of the abandoned Shihoro Line in Lake Nukabira — the 'phantom bridge' that surfaces and sinks with the reservoir; Japan Heritage.

P.n: Lake Shikaribetsu (然別湖)
P.ad: Shikaribetsu-kohan, Shikaoi, Katō District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's highest lake (810 m) and the only natural lake in Daisetsuzan National Park — canoeing in summer, an ice village with lake-ice onsen in winter.

P.n: Kōfuku Station (旧国鉄広尾線 幸福駅)
P.w: The closed Hiroo Line halt whose name means 'happiness' — the 'Ai-koku → Kōfuku' (from Love Country to Happiness) ticket made it a pilgrimage; old railcars and ticket-covered walls remain.

P.n: Rokkatei Art Village Nakasatsunai (六花亭 中札内美術村)
P.ad: Sakae-Higashi, Nakasatsunai, Kasai District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Rokkatei's oak-forest art village — four small museums, the sweets maker's restaurant and paths on old railway sleepers; free, late April–early November.

P.n: Manabe Garden (真鍋庭園)
P.w: Japan's first conifer garden — 83,000 m² of Japanese, Western and landscape gardens with thousands of trees from Northern Europe and Canada; on the Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.n: Tokachi Millennium Forest (十勝千年の森)
P.ad: Haobi, Shimizu, Kamikawa District (Tokachi), Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A forest planned to last a thousand years, with Dan Pearson's Earth, Meadow, Forest and Farm gardens — horse trekking and Segway tours; Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.n: Rokka no Mori (六花の森)
P.ad: Nishi 3-sen, Nakasatsunai, Kasai District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Rokkatei's 100,000 m² meadow of the 'Tokachi six flowers' painted on its wrapping paper, with small galleries of botanical art; Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.n: Mount Yōtei (羊蹄山)
P.ad: Kutchan / Makkari / Kyōgoku / Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 'Ezo-Fuji' — a near-perfect 1,898 m stratovolcano towering over the Niseko ski fields; its snowmelt feeds the Fukidashi springs.

P.n: Farm Tomita (ファーム富田)
P.ad: Kisen-kita, Nakafurano, Sorachi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The farm that kept Furano's lavender alive and made it famous — July's purple slopes and the striped 'Irodori' flower field under the Tokachi range. Free entry.

P.n: Ōkurayama Ski Jump Stadium & Sapporo Olympic Museum (大倉山ジャンプ競技場)
P.w: The 1972 Winter Olympics large hill — ride the chairlift to the top-of-jump observatory over the city, then the Olympic Museum at its foot.

P.n: Shiroi Koibito Park (白い恋人パーク)
P.w: Ishiya's Tudor-style chocolate factory behind Hokkaido's most famous souvenir cookie — factory line views, cookie workshops, a free courtyard and café.

P.n: Nijō Market (二条市場)
P.ad: Minami 3-jō Higashi 1–2-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A city block of crab, uni, ikura and fish stalls since the Meiji era, with kaisendon counters and the Noren Yokochō drinking alley.

P.n: Susukino (すすきの)
P.ad: Minami 4-jō – Minami 7-jō Nishi 2–6-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's biggest entertainment district north of Tokyo — the Nikka neon man, Ramen Yokochō, izakaya towers and the February ice-sculpture site.

P.n: Sapporo Curb Market — Jōgai Shijō (札幌場外市場)
P.ad: Kita 11-jō Nishi 21–22-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Around 60 stalls and seafood diners on the edge of the Central Wholesale Market — early-morning crab and kaisendon away from the downtown crowds.

P.n: Tanukikōji Shopping Street (狸小路商店街)
P.ad: Minami 2/3-jō Nishi 1–7-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's oldest shopping arcade (1873) — seven covered blocks of drugstores, souvenir shops, retro diners and the market at 7-chōme.

P.n: Bank of Japan Otaru Museum (日本銀行旧小樽支店金融資料館)
P.w: Tatsuno Kingo's 1912 branch of the Bank of Japan from the days Otaru was 'the Wall Street of the North' — now a free museum of money and the vault.

P.n: Mount Tengu, Otaru (天狗山)
P.w: Otaru's 532 m house mountain — a ropeway to a night view over the harbour and Ishikari Bay, and a ski hill in winter.

P.n: Otaru Herring Mansion, Shukutsu (鰊御殿)
P.w: A late-19th-century herring fishermen's lodge on the Shukutsu headland — the boss's quarters and bunk lofts from the herring boom that built Otaru.

P.n: Former Aoyama Villa — Otaru Kihinkan (小樽貴賓館 旧青山別邸)
P.w: The opulent 1923 retreat a herring-fishing dynasty built from its fortune — painted ceilings, lacquer and a peony garden.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — model for the herring-fishing boss's mansion in the Otaru arc · herring villa

P.n: Cape Kamui, Shakotan (神威岬)
P.ad: Kamuimisaki, Shakotan, Shakotan District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: An 80 m knife-edge cape on the Shakotan Peninsula — the 'Charenka trail' ridge walk to the lighthouse above 'Shakotan blue' sea.

P.n: Shimamui Coast, Shakotan (島武意海岸)
P.ad: Iridomari, Shakotan, Shakotan District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Through a short hand-dug tunnel to a cove of startling clear blue — one of Japan's '100 best beaches'.

P.n: Shikisai-no-Oka (四季彩の丘)
P.ad: Shinsei Daisan, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Biei's biggest flower hill — around 30 kinds of flowers in stripes over the rolling fields, with the Tokachi range behind.

P.n: Shirahige Waterfall (白ひげの滝)
P.ad: Shirogane Onsen, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Groundwater spilling from a cliff into the blue Biei River at Shirogane Onsen — the 'white beard' that tints the Blue Pond downstream.

P.n: Patchwork Road, Biei (パッチワークの路)
P.ad: Biei (northwest of the town centre), Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The quilt of wheat, potato and buckwheat fields made famous by TV ads — the Ken & Mary Tree, Seven Stars Tree and Hokusei Hill lookout.

P.n: Ginga Falls, Sōunkyō (銀河の滝)
P.ad: Sōunkyō, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 'Milky Way Falls', the slender twin of Ryūsei ('Shooting Star') Falls, ribboning down the 100 m basalt walls of the gorge.

P.n: Mount Kurodake & Kurodake Ropeway (黒岳)
P.ad: Sōunkyō, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Ropeway and chairlift from Sōunkyō to within an hour of the 1,984 m summit — the quickest way into Daisetsuzan's alpine plateau.

P.n: Ōfune Site — Jōmon (大船遺跡)
P.w: A Middle Jōmon village above the Pacific — more than 100 pit-dwelling hollows, some 2 m deep, part of the 2021 UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan.

P.n: Kakinoshima Site — Jōmon (垣ノ島遺跡)
P.w: A settlement where living and burial grounds were separated for millennia, with a 190 m U-shaped earthen mound; the Hakodate Jōmon Culture Center (with Hokkaido's only National Treasure, a hollow clay dogū) is beside it. UNESCO.

P.n: Washinoki Stone Circle (鷲ノ木遺跡)
P.ad: Washinoki-chō, Mori, Kayabe District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's largest stone circle (Late Jōmon), a double ring of stones on a hill above Uchiura Bay — an associated site of the Jōmon World Heritage nomination.

P.n: Kitakogane Shell Mound — Jōmon (北黄金貝塚)
P.w: A Jōmon settlement with large shell middens facing Uchiura Bay and a 'water site' where tools were ritually sent back — UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

P.n: Irie & Takasago Shell Mounds — Jōmon (入江・高砂貝塚)
P.ad: Takasago-chō, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Two Jōmon sites a few hundred metres apart above Uchiura Bay — the Irie village shell mound and the Takasago burial ground. UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

P.n: Kiusu Earthwork Burial Circles — Jōmon (キウス周堤墓群)
P.w: Ring-shaped earthen burial enclosures up to 75 m across in a Chitose forest — among the largest Jōmon communal cemeteries. UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

P.n: Shōwa-shinzan (昭和新山)
P.ad: Sōbetsu Onsen, Sōbetsu, Usu District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: One of the world's youngest mountains: a lava dome that rose out of a wheat field in 1943–45 to 398 m and still steams — beside the Usuzan Ropeway base.

P.n: Lake Kuttara (倶多楽湖)
P.w: A near-perfectly round caldera lake above Noboribetsu Onsen with no inflowing river — rated among Japan's clearest.

P.n: Niseko Annupuri (ニセコアンヌプリ)
P.ad: Niseko / Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1,308 m volcano whose flanks carry the Niseko United ski areas (Grand Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village, Annupuri) — famed for deep, dry powder and backcountry gates.

P.n: Shinsen-numa Pond (神仙沼)
P.ad: Maeda, Kyōwa, Iwanai District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The loveliest of the Niseko range's marsh ponds — a 20-minute boardwalk through alpine bog to still water ringed by Todo firs.

P.n: Fukidashi Park, Kyōgoku (ふきだし公園)
P.w: Mount Yōtei's snowmelt gushes out here after decades underground — one of Japan's biggest spring discharges; locals fill bottles at the source.

P.n: Sushiya-dōri — Otaru Sushi Street (寿司屋通り)
P.w: From Otaru Station toward Ironai: five or six big sushi houses and nearly twenty around them — Otaru has over a hundred places serving sushi.

P.n: Sapporo Maruyama Zoo (札幌市円山動物園)
P.w: Opened 1951 beside the Maruyama primeval forest — polar bears seen from an underwater tunnel, a new elephant house and Hokkaido wildlife.

P.n: Maruyama Park (円山公園)
P.w: The city's favourite hanami park at the foot of Mount Maruyama, beside Hokkaido Shrine — barbecue under the cherries in early May, red maples in autumn.

P.n: Hōheikan & Nakajima Park (豊平館・中島公園)
P.w: The 1880 white-and-ultramarine Western-style imperial guesthouse, an Important Cultural Property, in the downtown park with Shōbu pond, the Hassōan teahouse and Kitara concert hall.

P.n: Sapporo Art Park (札幌芸術の森)
P.w: A 40-ha forest campus with a sculpture garden of 70-plus outdoor works, the art museum and craft studios — glorious in autumn colour.

P.n: Takino Suzuran Hillside National Government Park (国営滝野すずらん丘陵公園)
P.w: Hokkaido's only national government park — flower hills, the Ashiribetsu waterfall and forest trails, a snow park in winter.

P.n: Old Public Hall of Hakodate Ward (旧函館区公会堂)
P.ad: Motomachi, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan (top of Motoizaka slope)
P.w: The blue-grey and yellow 1910 colonial-style assembly hall looking over the port from the top of Motoizaka — an Important Cultural Property.

P.n: Former British Consulate of Hakodate (函館市旧イギリス領事館)
P.w: The British consulate building of Hakodate's treaty-port era in Motomachi, now a city-run museum of the port's opening.

P.n: Goryōkaku Tower (五稜郭タワー)
P.w: The observation tower beside the fort — the only way to see Goryōkaku's five-pointed star from above.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy (2026 Hakodate collab: announcements by Hijikata's voice actor Nakata Jōji) · Love Live! Sunshine!! S2 ep 8 glass-floor scene · observation tower star fort

P.n: Hakodate Magistrate's Office (箱館奉行所)
P.ad: Goryōkaku Park, Goryōkaku-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Built by the Edo shogunate in the late Edo period inside Goryōkaku to oversee northern defence and foreign affairs; restored on its original site.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — Hijikata Toshizō photo panel and two character goshuin-style castle stamps in the 2026 'Golden Kamuy — Hakodate Dyed in Gold' collaboration · magistrate office reconstruction

P.n: Hachimanzaka Slope (八幡坂)
P.w: The straight, stone-curbed slope that runs from Motomachi straight down to the harbour — Hakodate's most photographed view, lit up in winter.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Love Live! Sunshine!! — Aqours walk Hachimanzaka in S2 eps 8–9 (Hakodate arc) · slope harbour view

P.n: Lake Onneto (オンネトー)
P.ad: Akan-chō, Ashoro, Ashoro District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: One of Hokkaido's 'three mystical lakes' at the western edge of Akan-Mashū — its colour shifts with the light under the volcano Me-Akan, whose lava dammed it.

P.n: Bihoro Pass (美幌峠)
P.ad: Route 243, Bihoro / Teshikaga border, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 525 m pass on Route 243 with the widest view over Lake Kussharo, Japan's largest caldera lake — sea of clouds at dawn.

P.n: Kaminoko Pond (神の子池)
P.ad: Kiyosato, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan (forest NE of Lake Mashū)
P.w: 'Child of the Gods' pond, fed underground from Lake Mashū — 12,000 tonnes a day of cobalt spring water that never freezes, sunken logs visible 5 m down.

P.n: Okhotsk Drift Ice Museum & Mt Tento Observatory (オホーツク流氷館)
P.ad: Mt Tento summit, Abashiri, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Real drift ice in a sub-zero room and a 360° rooftop view over the Sea of Okhotsk from the top of Mt Tento.

P.n: Cape Nosappu (納沙布岬)
P.w: The easternmost point of Hokkaido's mainland at the tip of the Nemuro Peninsula — Japan's earliest sunrise, looking out toward the Habomai islets.

P.n: Notsuke Peninsula (野付半島)
P.w: A long, hooked sand spit curling into the Nemuro Strait — ghostly salt-killed forests, seals and wildflowers.

P.n: Wakkanai Port North Breakwater Dome (稚内港北防波堤ドーム)
P.w: A 14 m-high arcade of columns built over five years to shelter travellers walking between the harbour and the railway station from waves and northern winds — a Hokkaido Heritage.

P.n: Sōya Hills & the White Road (宗谷丘陵)
P.w: Hills shaped in the last Ice Age behind Cape Sōya, rich in wild birds and alpine plants — the 'White Road' is paved with crushed scallop shells.

P.n: Cape Sukoton, Rebun (スコトン岬)
P.ad: Funadomari, Rebun, Rebun District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Rebun's northernmost point and trailhead of the island's 4- and 8-hour coastal hikes.

P.n: Momoiwa Observatory & Trail, Rebun (桃岩展望台)
P.ad: Motochi, Rebun, Rebun District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 'peach rock' dome above Motochi — alpine flowers with Rishiri-Fuji across the water along the ridge trail.

P.n: Himenuma Pond, Rishiri (姫沼)
P.ad: Oshidomari, Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A small pond in primeval forest whose still surface mirrors Rishiri-Fuji upside down — an 800 m boardwalk loop.

P.n: Ningle Terrace, Furano (ニングルテラス)
P.ad: Nakagoryō, Furano, Hokkaido, Japan (New Furano Prince Hotel grounds)
P.w: About fifteen log-cabin craft shops linked by boardwalks in the Furano forest — silver snowflake charms, woodcarving, leather; lantern-lit after dark.

P.n: Takushinkan Gallery, Biei (拓真館)
P.ad: Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan (former primary school)
P.w: Landscape photographer Shinzō Maeda's gallery of the Biei hills he made famous, in a converted primary school among birch groves.

P.n: Kawamura Kaneto Ainu Memorial Museum (川村カ子トアイヌ記念館)
P.w: Founded 1916 — Japan's oldest Ainu cultural museum, run by an Ainu family in the old Chikabumi kotan, with a reconstructed bamboo-grass cise house.

P.n: Hakuchō Ōhashi Bridge, Muroran (白鳥大橋)
P.ad: Muroran, Hokkaido, Japan (Route 37 across Muroran Port)
P.w: Eastern Japan's longest suspension bridge, spanning Muroran harbour — lit at night above the city's famous factory-night views.

P.n: Kitaichi Glass Hall No. 3 (北一硝子 三号館)
P.w: Kitaichi Glass's largest shop, on Sakaimachi — glassware arranged by theme, from tableware to animal figures with Hokkaido motifs, and a café.

P.n: Sapporo Pirka Kotan — Ainu Culture Promotion Center (サッポロピリカコタン)
P.w: 'Beautiful village in Sapporo' — some 300 Ainu garments and tools you may handle, made by Ainu artisans.

P.n: Sapporo Factory (サッポロファクトリー)
P.w: Shopping complex on the site of the first Sapporo Beer brewery — the original brick buildings plus a vast glass atrium, shops, restaurants and a cinema.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — stands on the site of the Meiji Kaitakushi brewery, the setting of the 'Sapporo Beer Factory' arc (2025 theatrical release) · brick brewery shopping

P.n: Hōheikyō Dam (豊平峡ダム)
P.w: A 102.5 m concrete arch dam (1972) on the upper Toyohira River beyond Jōzankei — autumn colour in the Jōzankei hills.

P.n: Yunokawa Onsen, Hakodate (湯の川温泉)
P.w: Hakodate's seaside hot-spring quarter, one of Hokkaido's three great onsen areas, with a history going back to 1653.

P.n: Otaru Aquarium (おたる水族館)
P.w: Hokkaido's largest aquarium (about 250 species) on the Shukutsu headland — seals and sea lions in pens sectioned off from the open sea.

P.n: Tokachigawa Onsen (十勝川温泉)
P.w: A rare 'moor' hot spring of plant-derived organic water, prized as a skin-softening bath, on the Tokachi River just outside Obihiro.

P.n: Naitai Highland Ranch & Naitai Terrace (ナイタイ高原牧場)
P.ad: Naitai, Kamishihoro, Katō District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's largest public ranch (est. 1972) rolling over Mount Naitai at the north-west edge of the Tokachi Plain — the terrace café looks out across the plain.

P.n: Cape Erimo (襟裳岬)
P.ad: Erimo, Horoizumi District, Hokkaido, Japan (Hidaka coast, south of Tokachi)
P.w: Where the Hidaka mountains run into the Pacific as a chain of reefs — a wind-blasted cape at the southern tip of the Hidaka range.

P.n: Catholic Motomachi Church (カトリック元町教会)
P.w: Founded 1859 by the French missionary Mermet-Cachon and rebuilt in Gothic style in 1924 — its altar is the only one in Japan given by a Pope.

P.n: Hakodate City Museum of Northern Peoples (函館市北方民族資料館)
P.w: Ainu and Okhotsk-coast peoples' clothing, tools and ritual objects — try Ainu paper-cutting or make and play traditional instruments.

P.n: Hakodate Jōmon Culture Center (函館市縄文文化交流センター)
P.w: Home of a National Treasure, the 3,500-year-old hollow clay dogū (41.5 cm) found by chance in 1975 — beside the UNESCO Kakinoshima site.

P.n: Trappist Monastery, Hokuto (トラピスト修道院)
P.w: Japan's first men's monastery (1896).

P.n: Kaiyō Maru replica & Kamome Island, Esashi (開陽丸・鴎島)
P.w: A full-size replica of the shogunate's Dutch-built flagship that sank off Esashi in a storm in 1868, moored at the entrance to Kamome Island in the herring-trade port.

P.n: Lake Akan Ainu Kotan (阿寒湖アイヌコタン)
P.ad: Akanko Onsen, Akan-chō, Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's largest Ainu settlement (about 120 residents) on Lake Akan — craft shops, the Ikor theatre's UNESCO-listed traditional dances and Ainu restaurants.

P.n: Cape Chikyū, Muroran (地球岬)
P.w: 100 m cliffs at the tip of the Etomo Peninsula with a white octagonal lighthouse and a sweep of the Pacific.

P.n: Cape Tachimachi (立待岬)
P.ad: South side of Mount Hakodate, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 30 m cliff on the south side of Mount Hakodate jutting into the Tsugaru Strait — on clear days the Shimokita and Tsugaru peninsulas of Aomori across the water.

P.n: Hokkaido Museum (北海道博物館)
P.ad: 53-2 Konopporo, Atsubetsu-chō, Atsubetsu-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The prefecture's museum of nature and history beside the Historical Village — five themes including Ainu culture, history and wildlife.

P.n: Lake Utonai (ウトナイ湖)
P.w: Japan's first bird sanctuary (1981) on the edge of Tomakomai — whooper swans and white-fronted geese stop over from autumn to spring.

P.n: Hokkaido Museum of Modern Art (北海道立近代美術館)
P.ad: Kita 1-jō Nishi 17-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's largest art collection — over 5,000 works by Hokkaido-linked masters (Kataoka Tamako, Iwahashi Eien, Kida Kinjirō, Kanda Nisshō) — next to the Hokkaido Governor's Official Residence.

P.n: Hakodate Tropical Botanical Garden (函館市熱帯植物園)
P.w: A pyramid greenhouse of tropical plants at Yunokawa — famous for the Japanese macaques soaking in their own hot-spring pool from December to May.

P.n: Noboribetsu Date Jidaimura (登別伊達時代村)
P.w: An immersive Edo-period theme park near Noboribetsu Onsen.

P.n: JR Tower Observatory T38 (JRタワー展望室 T38)
P.ad: JR Tower (Sapporo Station), Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 38th-floor deck of the Sapporo Station tower — a 360° view down the city grid to Ōdōri and the mountains.

P.n: Sapporo Dome (札幌ドーム)
P.w: The silver dome stadium of football and concerts, with an observatory over the city.

P.n: Niseko Tokyu Grand Hirafu (ニセコ東急 グラン・ヒラフ)
P.ad: Hirafu, Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The biggest of the Niseko United resorts on Annupuri's east face — powder runs, backcountry gates and the Hirafu village of restaurants and bars.

P.n: Niseko HANAZONO Resort (ニセコHANAZONOリゾート)
P.w: Grand Hirafu's satellite base on the north-east flank of Annupuri, reached by bus from Kutchan Station.

P.n: Rusutsu Resort (ルスツリゾート)
P.w: One of Hokkaido's best ski areas across three mountains — long groomers, powder and trees in winter; an amusement park with seven roller coasters, pools and onsen in summer.

P.n: Ueno Farm, Asahikawa (上野ファーム)
P.w: Gardener Ueno Sayuki's 'Hokkaido garden' — English planting blended with Furano-region wild nature; a mecca for Japanese gardeners on the Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.n: Kaze no Garden, Furano (風のガーデン)
P.ad: New Furano Prince Hotel grounds, Furano, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 2,000 m² English garden of 20,000 flowers grown over two years as the set of Kuramoto Sō's TV drama 'Kaze no Garden'.

P.n: Unkai Terrace, Hoshino Resorts Tomamu (雲海テラス)
P.ad: Tomamu, Shimukappu, Yūfutsu District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A gondola-top deck at 1,088 m above the Tomamu valleys — on calm mornings from May to October a white sea of clouds fills the Hidaka foothills.

P.n: Ikeda Wine Castle (池田ワイン城)
P.w: The town-run winery in a European-style castle — underground cellars of oak barrels, a brandy still, Tokachi wines and a top-floor restaurant over the Tokachi Plain.

P.n: Tokachi Hills (十勝ヒルズ)
P.w: Hilltop gardens over Tokachi built on 'flowers, food and farming' — seven theme gardens including 800 rose bushes, herbs, fruit trees and edible flowers.

P.n: Pokémon Center Sapporo (ポケモンセンターサッポロ)
P.ad: Daimaru Sapporo 8F, Kita 5-jō Nishi 4-7, Chuo-ku, Sapporo 060-0005, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's only official Pokémon Center, on the 8th floor of Daimaru by Sapporo Station — ~2,500 items incl. Sapporo-only Pikachu goods and pins.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon — the franchise's official flagship store for Hokkaido, with Sapporo-exclusive merchandise · character store

P.n: Hokuchin Memorial Museum, Asahikawa (北鎮記念館)
P.w: Free JGSDF museum at Camp Asahikawa on the Imperial Army's 7th Division and Meiji-era Asahikawa — uniforms and bayonets that Golden Kamuy fans come to see.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — the real 7th Division's museum; Noda Satoru's uniform references, a core fan pilgrimage · military history museum

P.n: Hakodate Arena (函館アリーナ)
P.w: Hakodate's arena by Yunokawa Onsen — the Love Live! regional-preliminary venue in Sunshine!! S2 and the real home of the 2018 Saint Snow-hosted Hakodate Unit Carnival.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Love Live! Sunshine!! — the Hakodate venue of the S2 regional preliminaries (Saint Snow's home city) · arena · anime pilgrimage

P.n: Snow Miku Sky Town, New Chitose Airport (雪ミク スカイタウン)
P.ad: Domestic Terminal 4F, New Chitose Airport, Chitose, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Shop-and-museum for Snow Miku, the white Hatsune Miku born from a 2010 Sapporo Snow Festival sculpture — life-size figure, illustrations, airport-only goods.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Hatsune Miku / Snow Miku — Sapporo-based Crypton's Hokkaido mascot Miku, with her permanent airport museum · character museum & shop

P.n: Mount Esan (恵山)
P.w: A still-steaming 618 m active volcano at the eastern tip of the Kameda Peninsula — trails from the 300 m crater-floor car park, and some 600,000 wild Ezo azaleas around Esan Tsutsuji Park.

P.n: Hokkaido-Komagatake (北海道駒ヶ岳)
P.w: The 1,131 m active volcano that symbolises southern Hokkaido — once a Fuji-like cone, its summit collapsed in the 1640 eruption, leaving jagged peaks such as Kengamine; climbable June–October.

P.n: Hakodate Park (函館公園)
P.w: A Meiji-era 4.8 ha park with an Ishikawa Takuboku poem stone, the city museum and Hokkaido's first stone bridge (about 10 m).

P.n: Hokkaido Hakodate Museum of Art (北海道立函館美術館)
P.ad: Beside Goryōkaku Park, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Southern Hokkaido's prefectural art museum next to Goryōkaku Park — a collection of over 2,500 works built on three themes: Dōnan art, calligraphy and contemporary art.

P.n: Tokachidake Bōgakudai Observatory (十勝岳望岳台)
P.ad: Mount Tokachi slopes, Daisetsuzan, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A lookout over Mount Tokachi's rugged volcanic terrain with views out toward Asahikawa and Furano, and a 1.1 km trail through volcanic rock and alpine flora.

P.n: Kamui Kotan (神居古潭)
P.w: 'Dwelling place of the gods' in Ainu — a gorge of the Ishikari River between green-schist cliffs carved over 100 million years; one of Asahikawa's Eight Scenic Views.

P.n: Lake Nukabira (糠平湖)
P.ad: Nukabira Gensenkyō, Kamishihoro, Katō District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A forest-ringed lake made in 1955 by damming the Otofuke River — the felled stumps on its bed raise 100+ 'mushroom ice' formations around February, and the Taushubetsu bridge surfaces from it.

P.n: Mikuni Pass Observatory (三国峠)
P.ad: Daisetsuzan National Park (Ishikari–Tokachi–Kitami border), Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's highest national-road pass at 1,139 m — a lookout over an endless sea of forest and the Matsumi Ōhashi bridge in Daisetsuzan National Park.

P.n: Arishima Memorial Museum (有島記念館)
P.ad: 有島57, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Literary museum opened in 1979 for Shirakaba-school writer Arishima Takeo on the farmland he owned — the setting of 'Cain's Descendants' — with a book café looking out on Mount Yōtei.

P.n: Hongō Shin Memorial Museum of Sculpture (本郷新記念札幌彫刻美術館)
P.ad: 宮の森4条12丁目, Chūō-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Museum for Sapporo-born Hongō Shin (1905–1980), a leading figure of postwar Japanese outdoor sculpture — 1,800 pieces including plaster models for his public works and sketches.

P.n: Fugoppe Cave (フゴッペ洞窟)
P.ad: 栄町87, Yoichi, Yoichi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A cave with over 800 Zoku-Jōmon engravings (c. 1,500–2,000 years old) — people, boats, fish and winged shamanic figures thought to be carved for ritual. Closed mid-Dec to early April.

P.n: Cape Noshappu (ノシャップ岬)
P.w: Wakkanai's westernmost point, jutting into the Sōya Strait — Ainu for 'where the cape juts out like a jaw', with views of Rishiri and Rebun and famous sunsets.

P.n: Noshappu Cold Current Aquarium (ノシャップ寒流水族館)
P.w: Japan's northernmost aquarium at Cape Noshappu — about 100 cold-water species incl. the 'phantom fish' itō in a 90-tonne circular tank; joint ticket with the adjacent Wakkanai Youth Science Museum.

P.n: Hokkaido University — Poplar & Ginkgo Avenues (北海道大学 札幌キャンパス)
P.ad: 7 minutes walk from JR Sapporo Station, Kita-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1876 Sapporo Agricultural College campus, 7 minutes from the station — the 1903 Poplar Avenue (replanted after the 2004 typhoon), the ginkgo avenue, and a 1929 scratch-tile museum of 3 million specimens.

P.n: Maeda Forest Park (前田森林公園)
P.w: A 1980s–90s landscape park whose 600 m-long, 15 m-wide canal runs dead straight toward Mt Teine.

P.n: Yurigahara Park (百合が原公園)
P.w: A 25.4 ha flower park of some 6,400 plant varieties — the World Lily Gardens and gardens built with sister cities Portland, Munich and Shenyang.

P.n: Hokkaido Governor's Official Residence (北海道知事公館)
P.w: A 1936 Mitsui villa, state property since 1953 — its lawn garden, with millennium-old pit-dwelling remains, is open year round.

P.n: Former Nagayama Takeshirō Residence (旧永山武四郎邸)
P.w: The c.1880 home of Hokkaido's second governor — a forerunner of pioneer-era houses joining a pure Japanese study and reception rooms to Western-style building.

P.n: Sapporo Satoland (サッポロさとらんど)
P.w: A 74.3 ha agricultural park of flower fields, farm animals and lawns — pick potatoes, onions and corn from mid-June to early November.

P.n: Hiraoka Park plum grove (平岡公園 梅林)
P.w: About 1,200 red and white plum trees — one of Sapporo's largest groves — whose May bloom draws some 100,000 visitors and announces spring.

P.n: Seikatei (清華亭)
P.ad: Kita 7-jō Nishi 7-chōme, Kita-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: An 1880 rest house built for Emperor Meiji's Hokkaido visit — a Western-style building blended with Japanese rooms; a city-designated cultural property.

P.n: Jōzankei Dam & Sapporo Lake (定山渓ダム・さっぽろ湖)
P.w: The 117.5 m dam of 1989 that formed deep-blue Sapporo Lake — look up at it from the downstream park, with a dam museum and seasonal inside tours.

P.n: Mount Hakken — Kannon-iwa (八剣山)
P.w: A 498 m jagged ridge on the way to Jōzankei — about an hour up with ropes on the steep upper half, for a 360° summit view.

P.n: Nusamai Bridge, Kushiro (幣舞橋)
P.ad: Over the Kushiro River from JR Kushiro Station, Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: One of Hokkaido's three famous bridges (1889, rebuilt 1976) with bronze statues of the four seasons — the stage for Kushiro's famous sunsets.

P.n: Kamuiwakka Hot Falls, Shiretoko (カムイワッカ湯の滝)
P.ad: Kamuiwakka River, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A river heated by the active Mt Shiretoko-Iō — wade upstream through warm water to falls whose basins are natural hot baths; 'Water of the Gods' in Ainu.

P.n: Asahibashi Bridge, Asahikawa (旭橋)
P.ad: Over the Ishikari River, Asahikawa, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 1932 steel arch (224.82 m) over the Ishikari — one of Hokkaido's Three Great Bridges and the only one still in its original form; a Hokkaido Heritage site.

P.n: Fukiage Onsen open-air bath, Kamifurano (吹上温泉 吹上露天の湯)
P.ad: Slopes of Mt Tokachi, Kamifurano, Sorachi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A free, wild open-air hot spring about 1,000 m up the flank of Mt Tokachi, kept up for anyone to soak in.

P.n: Biei Shirogane Onsen (白金温泉)
P.ad: Shirogane, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A quiet spa village at the foot of the Tokachidake range, named in 1950 for water 'as precious as platinum' — base for the Blue Pond and Shirahige Falls.

P.n: Mount Tarumae (樽前山)
P.ad: Southeast of Lake Shikotsu, Tomakomai / Chitose, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 1,041 m active volcano crowned by the lava dome of its 1909 eruption — about an hour from the 7th-station car park to the crater rim's 360° walk (the crater itself is off-limits).

P.n: Ōyunuma River Natural Footbath, Noboribetsu (大湯沼川天然足湯)
P.w: A free footbath in a steaming river fed by a ~130°C crater lake, through primeval forest about 30 minutes' walk from the park service centre.

P.n: Niseko Goshiki Onsen (ニセコ五色温泉)
P.ad: Between the Niseko Annupuri and Iwaonupuri trailheads, Niseko mountains, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 1930 mountain hot spring at 750 m, smelling of sulphur, whose free-flowing water shifts from clear to milky white — hence 'five colours'.

P.n: Niseko Yumoto Onsen & Ōyunuma (ニセコ湯本温泉・大湯沼)
P.ad: Foot of Mt Chisenupuri, Niseko mountains, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: At the foot of Chisenupuri — a bubbling mud-sulphur pond where you watch the hot spring welling up, with onsen lodges around it.

P.n: Banei Tokachi — Obihiro Racecourse (ばんえい十勝・帯広競馬場)
P.w: Home of ban'ei racing — heavy draft-horse racing, Tokachi's signature spectacle.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Silver Spoon (Gin no Saji) — Arakawa Hiromu's Tokachi farm-school manga features ban'ei racing; 'Silver Spoon Day' race collabs · Uma Musume collab 2022 · draft-horse racing

P.n: Obihiro Centennial City Museum (帯広百年記念館)
P.w: Obihiro's centennial museum of Tokachi's history.

P.n: Tsukigata Kabato Museum — former Kabato Prison (月形樺戸博物館)
P.w: Museum in the 1886 headquarters of Kabato Shūjikan, the Meiji convict prison whose inmates cleared the Ishikari valley — irons, cells and the real men behind several Golden Kamuy convicts.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — Kabato prison held the real models of 'Pirate' Bōtarō, forger Kumagishi Chōan and 'Lightning' Sakamoto; a fan pilgrimage stop · prison history museum

P.n: Nibutani Ainu Culture Museum, Biratori (平取町立二風谷アイヌ文化博物館)
P.w: Town museum in Nibutani, the Saru River heartland of Ainu culture — nationally designated Ainu tools, robes and boats, plus recordings of yukar epics.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Golden Kamuy — Nibutani hosted the official TV-anime × Biratori riddle tour (Oct–Nov 2025); Biratori is a 'Golden Kamuy × Hokkaido' campaign area · Ainu culture museum

P.n: Niseko Konbu Onsen (ニセコ昆布温泉)
P.ad: Niseko-Konbu Onsen, Rankoshi, Isoya District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A designated national health-resort onsen at the south-west foot of Annupuri — several inns, each with its own spring (bicarbonate to chloride).

P.n: Noboribetsu Bear Park (のぼりべつクマ牧場)
P.ad: Noboribetsu Onsen-chō (ropeway from the onsen town), Noboribetsu, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 7-minute ropeway up Mt Shihorei to ~100 Ezo brown bears — with the 'human cage' where people, not bears, are behind the bars.

P.n: Sendai-han Shiraoi Moto-Jin'ya Site & Museum (仙台藩白老元陣屋跡・資料館)
P.ad: Jin'ya-chō, Shiraoi, Shiraoi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: 1856 coastal-defence camp of the Sendai domain — a national historic site with earthworks in a 66,000 m² park and a museum of ~300 objects.

P.n: Usu Zenkō-ji Temple (有珠善光寺)
P.w: Said founded in 826 and named one of the shogunate's three official Ezo temples (1804) — a national historic site, Hokkaido Heritage, and a cherry 'flower temple' with its rock-splitting sakura.

P.n: Mt Sokuryō Observatory, Muroran (測量山展望台)
P.w: A 200 m hill named for the Meiji surveyors who planned the Sapporo road — 360° views over the port, Hakuchō Bridge and the steelworks; a Japan Night View Heritage site.

P.n: Hokkaido Museum of Northern Peoples, Abashiri (北海道立北方民族博物館)
P.ad: Mt Tento, Shiomi, Abashiri, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Japan's only museum of the circumpolar peoples — Ainu, Okhotsk culture, Inuit, Sámi — on Mt Tento near the drift-ice museum.

P.n: Moyoro Shell Mound & Site Museum, Abashiri (モヨロ貝塚・モヨロ貝塚館)
P.ad: Mouth of the Abashiri River, Kitamachi, Abashiri, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: National historic site of the seafaring Okhotsk culture (5th–9th c.) at the Abashiri river mouth, with burials, shell middens and a site museum.

P.n: Hosooka Observatory, Kushiro Marsh (細岡展望台)
P.ad: Tōro, Kushiro-chō, Kushiro District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The 'Taikanbō' — the classic view of the marsh with the Kushiro River's S-bends to the horizon and the Akan peaks behind; famed at sunset.

P.n: Cape Kiritappu (霧多布岬 / 湯沸岬)
P.ad: Tōbutsu, Hamanaka, Akkeshi District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Sheer cliffs on the Pacific where sea otters and seals are watched from the headland — Hamanaka's signature viewpoint.

P.n: Akan International Crane Center 'GRUS' (阿寒国際ツルセンター)
P.w: Winter feeding ground and research centre where red-crowned cranes dance on the snowfields at close range.

P.n: Cape Notoro, Abashiri (能取岬)
P.w: 40–50 m sea cliffs jutting into the Okhotsk with a lone lighthouse — a drift-ice lookout from late January to early March.

P.n: Meiji Park & Brick Silos, Nemuro (明治公園)
P.w: Site of Hokkaido's second state ranch (1875); its three 15 m red-brick silos are among Japan's largest — registered cultural property and modernization heritage.

P.n: Shunkunitai Sandspit, Nemuro (春国岱)
P.ad: Between Lake Fūren and Nemuro Bay, Nemuro, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: An 8 km sandspit with a rare pure forest of Sakhalin spruce on dunes, 3 km of rugosa roses and some of Hokkaido's best birding.

P.n: Michi-no-eki Nakasatsunai & Bean Museum (道の駅 なかさつない)
P.w: Flower-filled roadside station under the Hidaka range with seven eateries, a bean museum and a pioneer memorial hall — the gateway to the Nakasatsunai art village.

P.n: Shichiku Garden, Obihiro (紫竹ガーデン)
P.w: Shichiku Akiyo's 18,000-tsubo flower garden on the Tokachi plain — ~2,500 varieties and a fixture of the Hokkaido Garden Path.

P.n: Former Aikoku Station, Obihiro (旧国鉄広尾線 愛国駅)
P.w: The 'From Aikoku (Land of Love) to Kōfuku (Happiness)' ticket station of the closed Hiroo Line — now a small railway museum with an SL.

P.n: Wakkanai Fukukō Market (稚内副港市場)
P.w: Harbourside complex of seafood market, Hatoba Yokochō food stalls, the Minato no Yu onsen with sea views and a Karafuto history exhibit.

P.n: Otatomari Pond, Rishiri (オタトマリ沼)
P.ad: Numaura, Oniwaki, Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Rishiri's largest pond, ringed by Japan's northernmost Sakhalin-spruce forest, with Mt Rishiri reflected in still water.

P.n: Sapporo Concert Hall Kitara (札幌コンサートホールKitara)
P.ad: Nakajima Kōen 1-15, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Hokkaido's first dedicated concert hall and home of the Sapporo Symphony Orchestra — a glass-walled hall in Nakajima Park famed for its soft, deep acoustics.

P.n: Hokkaido University Museum (北海道大学総合博物館)
P.ad: Kita 10-jō Nishi 8-chōme, Kita-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 1929 scratch-tile campus building holding 3 million+ specimens gathered over 140 years — free, 10 minutes' walk from Sapporo Station.
s: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/北海道大学総合博物館

P.n: Migishi Kōtarō Museum of Art, Hokkaido (北海道立三岸好太郎美術館)
P.ad: Kita 2-jō Nishi 15-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Devoted to the Sapporo-born modernist painter who died at 31, with a reproduction of his atelier.
s: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/北海道立三岸好太郎美術館

P.n: Hokkaido Museum of Literature (北海道立文学館)
P.ad: Nakajima Kōen 1-4, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: Inside Nakajima Park: Hokkaido's literature from Ainu oral epics to Takiji Kobayashi and Ayako Miura — some 260,000 items.

P.n: Nopporo Forest Park (野幌森林公園)
P.w: 2,053 ha of lowland forest on Sapporo's edge — 17 trails through a wildlife sanctuary of Ezo squirrels and 150 bird species; the Hokkaido Museum and Historical Village sit at its edge.
s: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/道立自然公園野幌森林公園

P.n: Koganeyu Onsen (小金湯温泉)
P.w: A quiet 1883 hot-spring hamlet on the Toyohira River, 5 km short of Jōzankei — settlers found the water under a giant katsura tree.

P.n: ES CON FIELD HOKKAIDO — Hokkaido Ballpark F Village (エスコンフィールドHOKKAIDO)
P.ad: Hokkaido Ballpark F Village, Kitahiroshima, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: The Fighters' 2023 retractable-roof ballpark at the heart of a 32-ha 'F Village' — with TOWER 11's natural hot spring and sauna overlooking the field; parts open free on non-game days.

P.n: Sapporo Teine (サッポロテイネ)
P.w: Sapporo's largest ski area, 40 minutes from downtown, with two 1972 Winter Olympic runs — the Olympic torch still overlooks the city and the Sea of Japan.

P.n: Sapporo Kokusai Ski Resort (札幌国際スキー場)
P.w: Under an hour from the city yet with Niseko-rivalling snowfall — a 3.6 km forest trail and a 100 m-wide family run.

P.n: Sapporo City Astronomical Observatory (札幌市天文台)
P.ad: Nakajima Kōen 1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
P.w: A 1958 public observatory in Nakajima Park with a 20 cm refractor — free night-time stargazing on six evenings a month.

F.n: Menya Saimi (麺屋彩未)
F.w: The miso-ramen counter Sapporo queues for — three white misos over a clear pork-bone broth, a dab of grated ginger on the chāshū. Michelin Bib Gourmand (Hokkaido 2017) and Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100 (2024).

F.n: Sumire Susukino (すみれ 札幌すすきの店)
F.ad: Pixis Bldg 2F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 3-9-2, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The Murakami family house (1964) that codified the lard-sealed, scalding Sapporo miso bowl; the late-night Susukino branch pours the Nakanoshima honten broth. Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100 2024 & 2025.

F.n: MEN-EIJI Hiragishi Base (麺eiji 平岸base)
F.w: Additive-free broths and house-made noodles from Hokkaido wheat since 2006 — the gyokai-tonkotsu shōyu and the miso both draw lines. Michelin Bib Gourmand (Hokkaido 2017).

F.n: Jingisukan Daruma Honten (だるま本店)
F.ad: Crystal Bldg 1F, Minami 5-jō Nishi 4, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 064-0805, Japan
F.w: The Susukino jingisukan room since 1954 — a cast-iron dome at every seat, one cut of mutton, sweet-spicy dipping sauce, a queue from 17:30. Cash only.

F.n: Soup Curry Garaku (スープカレー GARAKU)
F.ad: Okumura Bldg B1F, Minami 2-jō Nishi 2-6-1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Numbered tickets and daily lines for a soup curry whose broth borrows udon-shop dashi technique — pork bone and herbs stewed two days, kelp and bonito layered in.

F.n: Soup Curry & Dining Suage+ (すあげ+)
F.ad: Minami 4-jō Nishi (〒064-0804), Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan — a few minutes from Susukino Station
F.w: Locals' favourite Susukino soup curry: skewered roast chicken, stewed pork and a pile of local vegetables, with rice cut with red rice. 11:30–22:00 daily.

F.n: Oiso, Nijō Market (二条市場 大磯)
F.ad: Sapporo Nijō Market, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The classic first stop in 'Sapporo's kitchen' — morning queues for donburi of sea urchin, salmon roe and crab, ¥2,000–3,000.

F.n: Donburi Chaya, Nijō Market (どんぶり茶屋)
F.ad: Sapporo Nijō Market, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Born in Nijō Market, a specialist with over fifty kaisendon — all-crab, all-shrimp, uni-ikura-crab-scallop-botan-ebi — plus grilled-seafood bowls.

F.n: Rojiura Curry SAMURAI Sakura (路地裏カリィ侍. 櫻)
F.w: Rich soup curry built on vegetables contracted from farmers in Shibetsu and Nayoro — the 'Samurai' chain's original back-alley style.

F.n: Ajisai Honten, Hakodate (函館麺厨房あじさい 本店)
F.w: Founded 1930, the name in Hakodate shio ramen: a clear broth of southern-Dōnan kelp with pork and chicken bone and rock salt. Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100.

F.n: Lucky Pierrot Bay Area Honten (ラッキーピエロ ベイエリア本店)
F.ad: Bay Area waterfront, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The 1987 original of Hakodate's own burger chain (17 shops in the city), done up as a merry-go-round in a forest — the No. 1 Chinese Chicken Burger, sweet-spicy karaage with house mayo, never made ahead.

F.n: Asahikawa Ramen Village (あさひかわラーメン村)
F.w: Eight of Asahikawa's best-known shops under one roof — the city's shōyu style: pork-bone and seafood double broth sealed under a film of lard, thin, firm, wavy noodles.

F.n: Ganso Butadon no Panchō, Obihiro (元祖豚丼のぱんちょう)
F.ad: In front of Obihiro Station, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The 1933 Obihiro shop credited with inventing butadon — sweet-soy charcoal-grilled pork on rice, the Tokachi soul food. The name is from the Chinese 'fan ting'.

F.n: Butadon no Tonta, Obihiro (ぶた丼のとん田)
F.w: Among Obihiro's most popular butadon counters; Michelin Bib Gourmand in the Hokkaido 2017 special edition.

F.n: Isezushi, Otaru (伊勢鮨)
F.w: Otaru's Michelin-starred sushi counter (Hokkaido guide one star), with a casual by-the-piece outpost inside Otaru Station.

F.n: Otaru Masazushi Honten (おたる政寿司 本店)
F.w: Founded 1938 on Otaru's Sushiya-dōri — the old guard of the city's sushi, as loved by locals as by visitors. 11:00–15:00, 17:00–21:00.

F.n: Soup Curry Picante, Kita 13-jō Honten (ピカンティ)
F.ad: Near Hokkaido University (Kita 13-jō), Kita-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: One of the founding soup-curry houses (1996), by Hokkaido University — vegetable-heavy curries with a choice of rich, light or shrimp-dashi broth.

F.n: Kushiro Washō Market (釧路和商市場)
F.w: Kushiro's 1954 indoor fish market of ~60 stalls, home of the katte-don — buy a bowl of rice, then walk the stalls choosing each topping.

F.n: Robata, Kushiro (炉ばた)
F.w: Seventy-plus years at the charcoal hearth in the city that claims to have invented robatayaki — counter seats only around the fire, fish grilled in front of you.

F.n: Sapporo Beer Garden (サッポロビール園)
F.ad: Higashi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan (beside the Sapporo Beer Museum)
F.w: Restaurants spread through the garden serve fresh-lamb jingisukan and seasonal Hokkaido produce with Sapporo draught — Kessel Hall does all-you-can-eat-and-drink.

F.n: Ganso Sapporo Ramen Yokochō (元祖さっぽろラーメン横丁)
F.w: The narrow Susukino alley of a dozen-plus tiny ramen counters, open into the small hours — the classic post-drinking miso bowl.

F.n: Kitakaro Sapporo Honkan (北菓楼 札幌本館)
F.ad: Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan (3 min walk from Ōdōri Park)
F.w: Kitakaro's flagship in a historic building long loved as the city library and an art museum — sweets shop plus a café serving the cake set with Hokkaido-milk soft-serve.

F.n: Hasegawa Store Bay Area (ハセガワストア ベイエリア店)
F.w: Hakodate's convenience-store institution: the yakitori bentō grilled to order — in southern Hokkaido 'yakitori' means pork.

F.n: Uni Murakami Hakodate Honten (うに むらかみ 函館本店)
F.ad: Morning-market streets, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan (5 min walk from Hakodate Station)
F.w: Restaurant of a sea-urchin wholesaler that long supplied Tsukiji and top sushi counters — sweet, additive-free raw uni in bowls and set meals.

F.n: Ramen Santouka Honten, Asahikawa (らーめん山頭火 本店)
F.w: Hitoshi Hatanaka's nine-seat 1988 shop that took Hokkaido ramen worldwide — a mild, low-salt white broth; the tokusei toroniku (pork-cheek) bowl.

F.n: Ramen no Hachiya Gojō Sōgyōten (ラーメンの蜂屋 五条創業店)
F.w: Since 1947: a pork-bone and dried-horse-mackerel double broth under burnt lard, with house noodles — the shop credited with Asahikawa's low-hydration noodle.

F.n: Baikōken Honten, Asahikawa (梅光軒 本店)
F.w: Founded 1969 — pork, chicken and seafood double broth, rich yet clean; first winner of the citizens' Asahikawa Ramen Grand Prize.

F.n: Obihiro Hageten Honten (帯広はげ天 本店)
F.w: Tempura and local-food house founded 1934, whose first chef Yano Shōroku helped devise the butadon sauce — marbled loin seared fast at high heat, a restrained sweet glaze.

F.n: Rokkatei Obihiro Main Store (六花亭 帯広本店)
F.w: The 1933 Tokachi confectioner's home store — the Marusei Butter Sandwich, crisp pies and assortments, with a second-floor kissa café.

F.n: Aji no Daiō Muroran Honten (味の大王 室蘭本店)
F.w: Serving its thick, rich curry ramen since opening in Muroran in 1971 — the bowl that made curry ramen the city's new local dish; house-made medium-thick curly noodles.

F.n: Niseko Takahashi Farm Milk Kobo (ニセコ高橋牧場 ミルク工房)
F.ad: Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan (near Niseko Village ski resort)
F.w: The dairy farm's own sweets shop facing Mount Yōtei — soft-serve, rice-flour roll cake and drinking yogurt from the farm's milk, with a vegetable-buffet restaurant and cheese workshop alongside.

F.n: Kani Ryōri Hyōsetsu no Mon (蟹料理の店 氷雪の門)
F.w: Sapporo's oldest crab specialist — king, snow and hairy crab as sashimi, charcoal-grilled, shabu-shabu and tempura.

F.n: Sapporo Kani Honke Ekimae Honten (札幌かに本家 札幌駅前本店)
F.ad: Near JR Sapporo Station, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Crab bought direct at the fishing grounds and served at fair prices in set courses, steps from Sapporo Station.

F.n: Sushi Zen Honten (すし善 本店)
F.w: The grand old name in Sapporo sushi — an all-hinoki house with several counters and private rooms, Hokkaido fish handled with Edomae technique.

F.n: Wakadori Jidai Naruto Honten (若鶏時代なると 本店)
F.w: Otaru's soul food since 1952: a half young chicken from Date, seasoned only with salt and pepper and fried at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes — crackling outside, juicy inside.

F.n: LeTAO Main Store, Otaru (ルタオ本店)
F.ad: East end of Sakaimachi Street, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Otaru's patisserie of record at the end of Sakaimachi — the Double Fromage, a baked-and-rare two-layer cheesecake of Hokkaido dairy, plus store-only sweets.

F.n: Torimatsu, Kushiro (鳥松)
F.w: Said to be the birthplace of zangi (1960) — chicken marinated in about ten seasonings, fried and eaten with a spiced sauce.

F.n: Restaurant Izumiya Sōhonten, Kushiro (レストラン泉屋 総本店)
F.w: Kushiro's yōshoku house since 1954 and home of the spakatsu — its meat sauce is the taste of the dish, now even sold retort-packed.

F.n: New Montblanc, Nemuro (ニューモンブラン)
F.w: The original escalope shop: the dish was born around 1963 at Nemuro's 'Montblanc' and carried on here by a former cook — butter rice under a pork cutlet and demi-glace.

F.n: Rishiri Ramen Miraku (利尻らーめん味楽)
F.ad: 67 Kutsugata-honmachi, Rishiri, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Island ramen that made the magazines and TV — scorched-soy broth built on generous Rishiri kelp; the Rishiri main shop was a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the Hokkaido special edition. Lunch 11:30–14:00.

F.n: Kikuyo Shokudō Honten, Hakodate Morning Market (きくよ食堂 本店)
F.ad: Hakodate Morning Market, Wakamatsu-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The morning-market donburi counter since 1956 — choose three of uni, ikura, scallop, salmon, botan shrimp and snow crab over rice cooked on charcoal. Opens 05:00 in season.

F.n: Gotōken Honten — Restaurant Sekkatei (五島軒本店 レストラン雪河亭)
F.ad: 4-5 Suehiro-chō, Hakodate, Hokkaido 040-0053, Japan (Gotōken head office / honten)
F.w: Hakodate's grand Western restaurant since 1879 — Russian dishes from its founding days, classic French, and the curry that made its name.

F.n: Mingei Kissa Poronno, Akan Ainu Kotan (民芸喫茶 ポロンノ)
F.ad: 4-7-8 Akanko Onsen, Akan-chō, Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan (inside the Ainu Kotan)
F.w: Ainu cooking inside Hokkaido's largest Ainu village — pocche-imo and the yuk (venison) set, with gyōja-ninniku, fiddleheads and mushrooms gathered by the staff and deer from local hunters.

F.n: Utoro Fishermen's Wives' Canteen (ウトロ漁協婦人部食堂)
F.ad: 117 Utoro-higashi, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan (by Utoro fishing port)
F.w: A 20-seat counter by the harbour run by local fishermen's wives — salmon landed at Utoro the same morning; queues out the door at lunch. Late April–late October.

F.n: Aji no Daiō Noboribetsu Onsen (味の大王 登別温泉店)
F.w: Noboribetsu's own bowl: 'hell ramen' whose heat climbs by 'chōme' levels from 0 — the record stands at 62. Lunch 11:30–15:00.

F.n: Aji no Sanpei (味の三平)
F.ad: Daimaru Fujii Central 4F, Minami 1-jō Nishi 3-chōme 2, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0061, Japan
F.w: Where miso ramen was born in 1955 — the owner took his cue from miso soup.

F.n: Sapporo Miso Ramen Senmonten Keyaki Susukino Honten (けやき すすきの本店)
F.w: The miso-only Susukino counter with a permanent queue — an unclouded broth of pork knuckle, stewing hen and vegetables simmered over ten hours.

F.n: Ramen Shingen Minami 6-jō (らーめん信玄 南6条店)
F.w: Line-out-the-door miso ramen whose broth is simmered for more than three days into something rounded and gentle.

F.n: Yuiga Dokuson, Furano (唯我独尊)
F.ad: Near Furano Station, Furano, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Furano's curry institution — 100% Hokkaido-egg omu-curry over a spicy roux of onions and carrots cooked down for three days with Furano vegetables.

F.n: Furano Cheese Factory (富良野チーズ工房)
F.w: Five natural cheeses from Furano milk, made behind glass you can watch through — the pioneering red-wine-infused Wine Cheddar; butter too.

F.n: Magic Spice Sapporo Honten (マジックスパイス 札幌本店)
F.ad: Hongō-dōri 8-chōme Minami 6-2, Shiroishi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The shop that named 'soup curry' — a broth of about twenty spices built on the idea that food is medicine, ordered by escalating heat levels.

F.n: Okushiba Shōten Ekimae Sōseiji (奥芝商店 駅前創成寺)
F.ad: Hokuren Bldg B1F, Kita 4-jō Nishi 1-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Soup curry rebuilt around a sweet, rich shrimp-head dashi, piled with Hokkaido vegetables — the chain's station-side temple-themed branch.

F.n: Sapporo Rakkyo Kotoni (札幌らっきょ 琴似店)
F.ad: Capitaine Kotoni 1F, Kotoni 1-jō 1-7-7, Nishi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Kotoni stalwart whose deep, concentrated broth is the one curry-heads graduate to.

F.n: Jingisukan Hitsujikai no Mise Itadakimasu (羊飼いの店 いただきます。)
F.ad: Minami 5-jō Nishi 5-1-6, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Susukino jingisukan run by an owner who took up shepherding to supply it — rare cuts of purebred Hokkaido Suffolk on the domed grill.

F.n: Tsukisappu Jingisukan Club (ツキサップじんぎすかんクラブ)
F.w: Fresh mutton over charcoal in clay braziers, at a ranch-side club that began in 1953 as members-only.

F.n: Shibetsu Barbecue (士別バーベキュー)
F.ad: Minami 3-jō Nishi 7-7, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Tanukikōji 7-chōme arcade grill counted among the city's best for rare Suffolk lamb from Shibetsu.

F.n: Otokoyama Sake Park, Asahikawa (男山 OTOKOYAMA SAKE PARK)
F.w: The 350-year-old 'Otokoyama' label's Asahikawa brewery and museum, reopened in 2024 as a sake park — Edo-era records, winter brewing on view, free tastings.

F.n: Takasago Shuzō, Asahikawa (高砂酒造)
F.w: Asahikawa's flagship brewery since 1899, maker of 'Kokushi Musō' — a direct shop with free tastings and a small museum; winter tours by reservation.

F.n: Kunimare Shuzō, Mashike (國稀酒造)
F.ad: Inaba-chō 1-17, Mashike, Mashike District, Hokkaido 077-0204, Japan
F.w: Japan's northernmost sake brewery, 140+ years in the herring port of Mashike — tour the stone kura, then taste three brewery-only sakes free.

F.n: Otaru Sankaku Market (小樽三角市場)
F.ad: Beside JR Otaru Station, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The triangular fish market beside Otaru Station — crab, scallops and sea urchin over the counter, and fishmonger-run donburi canteens like Takinami Shokudō.

F.n: Kita no Yatai, Obihiro (北の屋台)
F.ad: North-exit district of JR Obihiro Station, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The 50 m alley of twenty tiny stalls that started Japan's yatai-village revival — Tokachi beef, vegetables and cheese, elbow to elbow.

F.n: Hakodate Hikari no Yatai Daimon Yokochō (函館ひかりの屋台 大門横丁)
F.ad: Daimon district near JR Hakodate Station, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Twenty-six tiny bars and kitchens on 800 m² in the Daimon nightlife quarter by Hakodate Station — the city's hashigo-zake circuit.

F.n: Jiyōken (滋養軒)
F.w: A 1947 shio-ramen counter still cutting noodles daily on its original machine from flour, kansui, salt and egg — closes when the soup runs out.

F.n: Hakodate Men'ya Yūmin (函館麺屋ゆうみん)
F.w: An ~80-year-old Chinese kitchen by the station whose shio ramen is rounded out with rock salt and aromatic oil.

F.n: Hōran (鳳蘭)
F.w: A Daimon-district veteran whose pale, clear shio broth is nine parts pork bone to one part chicken.

F.n: Hakodate Shio Ramen Shinano (はこだて塩らーめん しなの)
F.w: Station-side shio ramen served until midnight — the late-night bowl after Daimon Yokochō.

F.n: Asaichi no Ajidokoro Chamu (朝市の味処 茶夢)
F.ad: Donburi Yokochō Ichiba, Wakamatsu-chō 9-15, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Donburi Yokochō counter piling sea urchin, salmon roe and scallop over rice from 7am.

F.n: Ikkatei Tabiji (一花亭 たびじ)
F.ad: Donburi Yokochō Ichiba, Wakamatsu-chō 9-15, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The early opener of Donburi Yokochō — seafood bowls from 6am, open every day.

F.n: Asaichi Akebono Shokudō (朝市あけぼの食堂)
F.ad: Donburi Yokochō Ichiba, Wakamatsu-chō 9-15, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Donburi Yokochō shokudō of seafood bowls and grilled fish for the market's breakfast crowd.

F.n: Ramen Sapporo Ichiryūan (ラーメン札幌一粒庵)
F.ad: Hokuren Bldg B1F, Kita 4-jō Nishi 1-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The station-side ramen shop most fixated on local sourcing — Hokkaido wheat noodles, Hokkaido pork bones and vegetables, miso made to order.

F.n: Menya Yukikaze Susukino Honten (麺屋 雪風 すすきの本店)
F.w: No. 3 in MAPPLE's Sapporo ramen top 30 — a rich-yet-clean 'nōkō miso' of pork-bone and chicken paitan with curly medium noodles.

F.n: Ebisoba Ichigen Sōhonten (えびそば一幻 総本店)
F.w: Sapporo's prawn-ramen original, burning through ~60 kg of shrimp heads a day; pick your broth from pure shrimp to half pork-bone.

F.n: Parfait, Coffee, Sake, Satō Honten (パフェ、珈琲、酒、佐藤 本店)
F.ad: Kino Ninary Bldg 1F–3F, Minami 1-jō Nishi 2-chōme 1-2, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0061, Japan
F.w: The flag-bearer of Sapporo's 'shime parfait' — the night-capping parfait — with Hokkaido-milk ice cream, sorbets and bakes all made in-house; open till midnight.

F.n: INITIAL Sapporo
F.ad: F.DRESS Gogai Bldg 2F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 5-chōme 36-1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A pioneer of the night-parfait boom built on 'dessert and alcohol marriage' — sculptural parfaits till midnight, three minutes from Susukino.

F.n: Otaru Ankake-dokoro Tororian (小樽あんかけ処 とろり庵)
F.w: The ankake-yakisoba specialist run by the old Abe noodle mill — crisp-fried noodles under a thick, generous seafood-and-vegetable sauce.

F.n: Chūka Shokudō Keien (中華食堂 桂苑)
F.w: An arcade Chinese diner packed even on weekdays for the city's soul-food plate of fried noodles under thick ankake.

F.n: Kōzushi (幸寿司)
F.w: Tucked down an alley off Sushiya-dōri — a meticulous third-generation counter with nigiri sets from about ¥2,000.

F.n: Asahikawa Rāmen Aoba Honten (旭川らぅめん青葉 本店)
F.ad: Nijō Bldg Meitengai 1F, Nijō-dōri 8-chōme, Asahikawa, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A 1947 original kept by its third-generation master — the Asahikawa double soup of sea and land stocks in a lard-sealed shōyu bowl.

F.n: Miso Rāmen no Yoshino Honten (みそラーメンのよし乃 本店)
F.w: The trailblazer of Asahikawa miso ramen, miso-only since the day it opened.

F.n: Curry no Furanoya (カレーのふらのや)
F.w: A log-house curry shop near Furano Station with soup and roux curries built on local vegetables — a Furano lunch queue.

F.n: Kashi Kōbō Furano Delice (菓子工房フラノデリス)
F.w: A hillside patisserie using Furano milk and eggs — the bottled Furano milk pudding has sold out since day one; twenty-plus cakes daily.

F.n: Tokachi Butadon Ippin Honten (十勝豚丼 いっぴん本店)
F.w: A butadon house the locals rate with the founders — thick pork loin grilled and glazed in a sweet-soy tare over Tokachi rice.

F.n: Curry Shop Indian Machinaka (カレーショップ インデアン まちなか店)
F.w: Tokachi's beloved curry counters, run by the Fujimori group — locals bring their own pots for take-out; this is the downtown branch.

F.n: Ryūgetsu Sweetpia Garden, Otofuke (柳月スイートピア・ガーデン)
F.ad: Natsuzora 1-1, Otofuke, Katō District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Tokachi confectioner Ryūgetsu's factory park — watch the production line, then the cake shop and café.

F.n: Kushiro Rāmen Kawamura (釧路ラーメン 河むら)
F.w: The mainstream of Kushiro ramen: a crystal-clear, bonito-led shōyu soup and fine curly noodles, served into the Suehiro nightlife hours.

F.n: Kushiro Fisherman's Wharf MOO & Ganpeki Robata (釧路フィッシャーマンズワーフMOO・岸壁炉ばた)
F.ad: At the foot of Nusamai Bridge, Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Kushiro's harbour hall by Nusamai Bridge — a fish market downstairs, the retro 'Minato no Yatai' upstairs, and in summer the open-air quayside robata where you grill your own catch.

F.n: Akkeshi Mikaku Terminal Conchiglie — Michi-no-eki Akkeshi Gourmet Park (厚岸味覚ターミナル コンキリエ)
F.w: The roadside station of Japan's year-round oyster town — oyster restaurants, a grill-it-yourself seafood shop and oyster sweets above Akkeshi Bay.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Utoro Shiretoku restaurant (道の駅うとろ・シリエトク)
F.ad: Utoro, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The Utoro roadside station's local-catch restaurant: spring tokishirazu, summer pink salmon, autumn-winter prime chum — Shiretoko seafood at fair prices.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Bōyō Nakayama, Nakayama Pass (道の駅 望羊中山)
F.ad: Nakayama Pass (Route 230), Kimobetsu, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The pass-top stop where Sapporo drivers first see Mt Yōtei — famous for battered, fried Danshaku potatoes from the Yōtei foothills, plus Nakayama chicken and Rusutsu-pork butadon.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Niseko View Plaza (道の駅 ニセコビュープラザ)
F.w: Niseko's roadside farm market — local vegetables and fruit straight from the growers, handmade ham and ice cream, with Yōtei and Annupuri views.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Akaigawa (道の駅 あかいがわ)
F.ad: Maple Kaidō, Akaigawa, Yoichi District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A newer roadside station on the Maple Kaidō between Kiroro and Niseko — bread baked on site from local ingredients, Akaigawa milk, and gelato made with the village's rice.

F.n: Marutoma Shokudō, Tomakomai (マルトマ食堂)
F.w: A fishermen's diner facing Tomakomai harbour, open from 5am — Japan's top surf-clam port served as a heaped hokki curry and seafood bowls.

F.n: Yakitori no Ippei Nakajima Honten, Muroran (やきとりの一平 中島本店)
F.w: The shop that put Muroran 'yakitori' — charcoal pork and onion, eaten with hot mustard — on the national map by winning the Yakitorimpic twice.

F.n: MORIHICO. Main Store, Maruyama (森彦)
F.ad: Maruyama area, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The ivy-covered old timber house near Maruyama where Hokkaido's leading coffee brand began — dark home-roast hand-drip and house cakes.

F.n: Baristart Coffee, Ōdōri (バリスタートコーヒー)
F.ad: Edge of Ōdōri Park, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A 2015 Hokkaido-born stand that builds each latte around farm-direct milk — pick your dairy, led by Biei Jersey.

F.n: Bar Yamazaki, Susukino (BARやまざき)
F.ad: Katsumi Bldg 4F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 3-3, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Susukino's authentic bar since 1958, founded by one of Japan's longest-serving bartenders — order the vodka 'Sapporo' and leave with a paper-cut silhouette of your profile.

F.n: Jazz Café Bossa, Tanukikōji (ジャズ喫茶 BOSSA)
F.w: A Tanukikōji jazz kissa open since 1971 whose owner's 15,000 records and CDs have carried Sapporo's jazz scene for half a century.

F.n: Miyoshino Tanukikōji (みよしの 狸小路店)
F.ad: Minami 3-jō Nishi 2-chōme 16-4 (Tanukikōji 2-chōme), Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Sapporo's own gyoza-and-curry chain — the cult combo plate of six dumplings beside a pool of curry rice.

F.n: Nakamuraya, Shakotan (中村屋)
F.w: An uni fisherman's own shop: additive-free sea urchin landed that morning, with a ten-a-day bowl comparing bafun (red) and murasaki (purple) uni in season.

F.n: Shokudō Ushio, Shakotan (食堂 うしお)
F.w: A half-century seaside canteen buying uni straight from the fishermen and serving it untreated, with the cape's blue water out the window.

F.n: Oshokujidokoro Misaki, Shakotan (お食事処 みさき)
F.ad: Near Cape Kamui, Shakotan, Shakotan District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Fisherman-run at the tip of the peninsula — the owner is out for uni at 4am, and the limited bafun bowl sells out daily in season.

F.n: Tanaka Shuzō Kikkōgura, Otaru (田中酒造 亀甲蔵)
F.w: An 1899 brewery in a stone warehouse that brews all four seasons thanks to Hokkaido's cool climate — walk the brewery, then taste free.

F.n: Otaru Sōko No.1 — Otaru Beer (小樽倉庫No.1)
F.w: A brewpub inside a canal-side stone warehouse with the brewery on view — lagers from German organic barley and Otaru's soft water, with German-style plates.

F.n: Niikuraya Hanazono Honten, Otaru (新倉屋 花園本店)
F.w: An 1895 wagashi house whose Hanazono dango wear their red-bean paste in a single mountain-shaped sweep.

F.n: Amatō, Otaru (あまとう)
F.w: A Shōwa-era Otaru sweet parlour still loved for its cream zenzai.

F.n: California Baby, Hakodate (カリフォルニアベイビー)
F.ad: Bay area below Mt Hakodate (Motomachi side), Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A diner in a converted Taishō-era post office that nearly every Hakodate local has eaten at — the Cisco rice was the owner's riff on chili beans from his time in America.

F.n: Numa no Ya, Ōnuma (沼の家)
F.ad: Ōnuma, Nanae, Kameda District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Founded in 1905: unskewered dumplings laid in a box to echo the lakes and their ~126 islets, in bean paste and soy.

F.n: Hakodate Beer (はこだてビール)
F.w: The city's brewery restaurant on Kaikō-dōri — six regular beers on tap and a menu running from seafood to meat.

F.n: Hakodate Beer Hall, Kanemori (函館ビヤホール)
F.ad: Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse — Hakodate History Plaza, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A retro beer hall inside the Kanemori red-brick warehouses — two local beers, long sausage pie and potato-cheese bakes.

F.n: Kaisen-dokoro Kafuka, Rebun (海鮮処かふか)
F.ad: Kafuka, Rebun, Rebun District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The fishery co-op's own restaurant at Kafuka port — island sea urchin over rice and fat Rebun hokke, open for the summer season.

F.n: Robata Chidori, Rebun (炉ばた ちどり)
F.w: A Rebun robata where the local catch is miso-grilled at the hearth — the island's hokke chanchan-yaki is the order.

F.n: Fujiya NOODLE, Susukino (ふじ屋 NOODLE)
F.w: A seven-seat Susukino counter that won a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2017 Hokkaido edition and still draws the ramen obsessives.

F.n: Kaisen Shokudō Kita no Gourmet-tei, Curb Market (海鮮食堂 北のグルメ亭)
F.ad: Sapporo Central Wholesale Market — Jōgai Shijō, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The Curb Market's longest-running big canteen-cum-shop — its signature bowl lays twelve oversized toppings over rice.

F.n: Marusan-tei, Curb Market (まるさん亭)
F.ad: Sapporo Central Wholesale Market — Jōgai Shijō, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Run by crab-and-seafood wholesaler Marusan Mikami Shōten — about eight seasonal toppings (tuna, uni, scallop, salmon) heaped on one bowl.

F.n: Kaisen-dokoro Uoya no Daidokoro, Nijō Market (海鮮処 魚屋の台所)
F.ad: Nijō Market, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Nijō Market bowl shop opened by a long-time sushi chef to sell the freshest fish at fair prices — No. 2 in a MAPPLE readers' seafood ranking.

F.n: Biei Senka (美瑛選果)
F.w: JA Biei's food hall of morning-picked vegetables and limited Biei-wheat bread, with the French restaurant Asperges cooking the town's produce next door.

F.n: ROYCE' Chocolate World, New Chitose Airport (ロイズチョコレートワールド)
F.ad: New Chitose Airport 3F, Chitose, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Japan's first chocolate factory inside an airport — watch ROYCE' bite-size chocolates being made, then the shop and bakery.

F.n: Wakasaimo Honpo Tōyako Honten (わかさいも本舗 洞爺湖本店)
F.ad: Tōyako Onsen 144, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The lakeside flagship of Tōya's signature sweet, with the Sendō-an Japanese restaurant upstairs looking over the lake.

F.n: Cranberry Honten, Obihiro (クランベリー 本店)
F.w: Obihiro's handmade-cake house, famous for its sweet-potato cake and for letting each ingredient's own flavour lead.

F.n: Masuya Shōten Honten, Obihiro (満寿屋商店 本店)
F.w: 'Masuya-san' — the 100%-Tokachi-wheat bakery with seven shops in the region; the main store keeps the sweet, soft breads first baked as farmhands' snacks.

F.n: Nanbantei, Kushiro-chō (南蛮酊)
F.ad: Tōya 1-39, Kushiro-chō, Kushiro District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The home of 'zantare': fresh-fried chicken thigh doused in a soy-sugar-vinegar sauce, in portions big enough that take-home boxes are standard; weekend queues.

F.n: Satō Shokudō, Rishiri (さとう食堂)
F.ad: In front of the ferry terminal, Rishiri Island, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The long-running ferry-front canteen for Rishiri sea urchin over rice, grilled hokke sets and kelp ramen — open with the ferry season.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Mukawa Shiki no Yakata (道の駅 むかわ四季の館)
F.w: The roadside station of Japan's shishamo town — its Tanpopo dining room serves the local smelt in season.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Sarufutsu Kōen (道の駅 さるふつ公園)
F.w: On the Okhotsk coast of Japan's scallop capital — scallop curry in the restaurant and the station's own scallop-rice bento.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Shikabe Kanketsusen Kōen (道の駅 しかべ間歇泉公園)
F.w: A roadside station built around a geyser that blows about 15 m every 10–15 minutes — buy seafood and vegetables and steam them yourself in the hot-spring steam, then Shikabe cod roe at the Hama no Kaa-san canteen.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Pia 21 Shihoro (道の駅 ピア21しほろ)
F.w: The barn-roofed food hub of a beef-and-potato town — the Nijiiro Shokudō serves Shihoro beef steak with the town's vegetables.

F.n: Michi-no-eki 230 Rusutsu (道の駅 230ルスツ)
F.ad: Route 230, Rusutsu, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Rusutsu growers' farm stand on Route 230 — asparagus, corn and tomatoes picked that morning in high season, and a pizza counter visitors detour for.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Makkari Flower Center (道の駅 真狩フラワーセンター)
F.w: Makkari grows about 60% of Japan's edible lily bulbs — the station sells them fresh and baked into monaka and castella, under Mt Yōtei.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Nanairo Nanae (道の駅 なないろ・ななえ)
F.w: Nanae's food-and-history station, in the birthplace of Western-style farming in Japan — guaraná soft-serve from the local soda maker and croquettes of Yamakawa ranch beef.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Ryūhyō Kaidō Abashiri (道の駅 流氷街道網走)
F.w: Abashiri's roadside station — the Kinema-kan food court does local-only dishes like the pink-salmon-and-yam Abashiri burger.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Mashū Onsen (道の駅 摩周温泉)
F.w: The Teshikaga stop for Lake Mashū — Ezo-deer burgers and local dairy ice cream alongside the area's produce.

F.n: Hakodate Asaichi Ekini Ichiba (函館朝市 えきに市場)
F.ad: Hakodate Morning Market, by JR Hakodate Station, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The Morning Market hall with the squid-fishing tank — hook a live squid and the stallholder slices it into translucent sashimi with ginger soy at the table.

F.n: Hakodate Kaisen Ichiba Honten (はこだて海鮮市場 本店)
F.w: A big Bay-area seafood market of crab, squid and roe for tasting and shipping home.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Utonai-ko (道の駅 ウトナイ湖)
F.ad: Beside Lake Utonai, Tomakomai, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Beside Lake Utonai — a farm-and-fish shop and restaurant serving Tomakomai's hokki curry and the city's half-century-old miso-curry ramen.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Biei Shirogane Birke (道の駅 びえい「白金ビルケ」)
F.ad: Shirogane, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A birch-wood station at the Blue Pond gateway — burgers on Biei-wheat buns with premium patties, a bakery and Blue-Pond-themed treats.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Mochigome no Sato ☆ Nayoro (道の駅 もち米の里☆なよろ)
F.w: Nayoro's rice-country station — its own fluffy 'soft daifuku', made from local mochi rice in some eighteen flavours.

F.n: Restaurant Bōyōtei, Tōyako Onsen (レストラン望羊蹄)
F.ad: Tōyako Onsen 36-12, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido 049-5721, Japan
F.w: A 1946 Western-food house in Tōyako Onsen still cooking to its original recipes — named for the view of Mt Yōtei it once had; the hamburg set is the order.

F.n: Curry Shop S, Susukino (カレーショップ S)
F.ad: Silver Bldg B1F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 4-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A basement soup-curry counter in the middle of Susukino, on both the city tourism board's and GoodLuckTrip's Susukino lists.

F.n: Umi Hachikyō Honten, Susukino (海味はちきょう 本店)
F.ad: Miyako Bldg 1F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 3, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Susukino seafood izakaya, open 365 days a year until midnight.
