F.n: Night Parfait Nanakamado (夜パフェ専門店 ななかまど)
F.ad: Dai-4 Fujii Bldg 2F, Minami 4-jō Nishi 5-10, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A dedicated night-parfait bar in Susukino — the after-dinner, after-drinks parfait until late.

F.n: Parfaiteria PaL (パフェテリア パル)
F.w: A second night-parfait specialist in Susukino, open every night of the year until midnight or later.

F.n: Kiwami Shio-Jukusei Jingisukan Yūhi, Susukino (極 塩熟成ジンギスカン 夕陽)
F.w: A Susukino jingisukan specialising in salt-aged lamb, on both the city tourism board's shop list and GoodLuckTrip's Hokkaido jingisukan twelve.

F.n: Rokkatei Sapporo Honten (六花亭 札幌本店)
F.ad: 5 minutes' walk from JR Sapporo Station (south exit), Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Tokachi confectioner Rokkatei's Sapporo flagship — the shop below, and a café above serving store-only desserts; home of the Marusei Butter Sand (white chocolate, raisins, Hokkaido butter).

F.n: Kinotoya Ōdōri Kōen & KINOTOYA Café (きのとや 大通公園店)
F.ad: Ōdōri Kōen area, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Sapporo patissier Kinotoya's Ōdōri café — the fresh, silky milk soft-serve that topped New Chitose Airport's ice-cream election two years running.

F.n: Ōdōri BISSE (大通ビッセ)
F.ad: Directly connected to Ōdōri subway station, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A station-linked complex whose ground floor gathers famous Hokkaido confectioners and farm-milk soft-serve and gelato counters.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Space Apple Yoichi (道の駅 スペース・アップルよいち)
F.w: Yoichi's roadside station in apple country — orchard juice, house-made ice cream and apple pie from local fruit.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Misogi no Sato Kikonai (道の駅 みそぎの郷 きこない)
F.ad: At JR Kikonai Station (Hokkaido Shinkansen), Kikonai, Kamiiso District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The roadside station at the first Hokkaido Shinkansen stop — sweets and bread built on the salt of Kikonai's midwinter Kanchū Misogi festival, and the town's own sake.

F.n: Kushiro Rāmen Maruhira (釧路ラーメン まるひら)
F.w: A 60-plus-year Kushiro counter with a two-item menu, shōyu or shio, open mornings to early afternoon — No. 66 in Ramen Adventures' Hokkaido top 100.

F.n: Uocchi Rāmen Kōbō, Tanchō Market (魚一らーめん工房)
F.w: A Kushiro market ramen counter whose soup layers niboshi and kombu with its own saury and herring fish sauce.

F.n: Tsuruya, Asahikawa (つるや)
F.w: A downtown Asahikawa ramen shop ranked No. 40 in Ramen Adventures' 2024 Hokkaido top 100.

F.n: Kama-ei Factory Store, Otaru (かま栄 工場直売店)
F.w: Otaru's kamaboko house since 1905 — the pan-roll is, sold only here because it can't be shipped; café on site.

F.n: Kitaichi Hall, Otaru (北一ホール)
F.ad: Kitaichi Glass No. 3 building, Sakaimachi 7-26, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The café in Kitaichi Glass's Meiji stone warehouse, lit by 167 oil lamps that staff light one by one after the 9am opening.

F.n: Sushi-dokoro Kihara, Yunokawa (鮨処 木はら)
F.ad: Yunokawa Onsen area, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Yunokawa sushi counter whose chef grew up in a fishing family and buys the day's best catch — serious sushi without ceremony.

F.n: Soba-dokoro Fukuan, Noboribetsu Onsen (そば処 福庵)
F.w: An old-style soba shop opposite the Sagiri-yu public bath — Hokkaido buckwheat in hand-cut and machine-cut versions, lunch only.

F.n: Sabō Kikuizumi, Motomachi (茶房 菊泉)
F.w: Wagashi café in a Taishō-era sake merchant's villa — grill your own dango at the table — and the family home of Saint Snow's Kazuno sisters in Love Live! Sunshine!!, with collab goods on sale.
F.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Love Live! Sunshine!! — the Kazuno sisters' (Saint Snow) family home in S2 eps 8–9; a stop on the HOKKAIDO LOVE! location stamp rally

F.n: Sapporo Junren, Sapporo-ten (さっぽろ純連 札幌店)
F.w: The 1964 shop that set the rich, lard-sealed Sapporo miso style — rurubu calls it the long-running origin of the modern miso bowl.

F.n: Ajanta Yakuzen Curry Honpo Sōhonke (アジャンタ薬膳カリィ本舗総本家)
F.ad: Kita 23-jō Higashi 20-2-18, Higashi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Ajanta's 1970s medicinal curry is where Sapporo soup curry began; this is the head shop.

F.n: Soup Curry Yellow (スープカリーイエロー)
F.ad: Elm Bldg 1F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 1-12-19, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A 1996 soup-curry house with a clear pork-and-chicken stock and a 20-step heat scale.

F.n: Chitose-tsuru Sake Museum (千歳鶴 酒ミュージアム)
F.ad: Minami 3-jō Higashi 5-1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The shop and small museum of Sapporo's only sake brewery (Nihon Seishu), with free tasting counter and brewery-only bottles.

F.n: Snow Brand Parlor Sapporo Honten (雪印パーラー 札幌本店)
F.ad: Taiyō Seimei Sapporo Bldg 1F, Kita 2-jō Nishi 3-1-31, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Sapporo's 1961 dairy parlour: 30-plus parfaits and the 'Snow Royal' ice cream first made for a 1968 imperial visit.

F.n: Sapporo Senshūan Honten (札幌千秋庵 本店)
F.ad: Minami 3-jō Nishi 3, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Confectioner since 1921, maker of the Northman bean-paste pie and Yama-oyaji biscuits.

F.n: Miyakoshiya Coffee Honten, Maruyama (宮越屋珈琲 本店)
F.ad: Minami 2-jō Nishi 28, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Sapporo's best-known kissaten roaster; the first-floor windows look onto Maruyama Park.

F.n: Do Ermitage, Susukino (ドゥ・エルミタアヂュ)
F.ad: Minami 3-jō Nishi 4 Bldg 10F, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: An old-school authentic bar run by a woman with about 50 years behind the counter; more than 400 whiskies.

F.n: Jingisukan Yōyōtei Sapporo Honten (ジンギスカン羊々亭 札幌本店)
F.w: Specialist lamb grill known for its rare 'Roaring Forties' lamb.

F.n: Nama-Ramu Jingisukan Yamagoya, Susukino (生ラムジンギスカン 山小屋)
F.ad: Dai-5 Green Bldg 1F, Minami 4-jō Nishi 4-13-2, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Susukino fresh-lamb grill carrying on the 1956 sauce of Otaru's Keishōen.

F.n: Beer Bar North Island (ビアバー ノースアイランド)
F.ad: Large Country Bldg 10F, Minami 2-jō Nishi 4-10-1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Taproom of Sapporo's North Island Beer (founded 2003, now brewed in Ebetsu) — fresh kegs, guest and seasonal beers.

F.n: Moon and Sun Brewing (月と太陽BREWING)
F.w: A brewpub on the city's craft-beer trail.

F.n: Misoramen Senmonten Ōkami Soup (味噌らーめん専門店 狼スープ)
F.ad: Near Nakajima Park, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Started as a yatai in 2000 and reopened in 2012; it serves miso ramen only.

F.n: Kiraito, Tanukikōji (喜来登)
F.ad: Minami 2-jō Nishi 6, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A Tanukikōji miso ramen shop that fries the vegetables and garlic in the wok before the soup goes in, the old Sapporo way.

F.n: Otaru Wine Gallery — Hokkaido Wine Otaru Winery (北海道ワイン おたるワインギャラリー)
F.w: Hokkaido Wine's head winery (founded 1974): a tasting bar with about 100 wines and paid winery tours.

F.n: Soba-ya Yabuhan, Otaru (蕎麦屋 籔半)
F.w: A 1954 Edo-style soba house near Otaru Station.

F.n: Ice Cream Parlor Misono, Otaru (アイスクリームパーラー美園)
F.w: Opened in 1919 as the first shop in Hokkaido to sell ice cream, and still uses its original method.

F.n: Uomasa, Otaru (魚真)
F.w: Local-catch sushi at fair prices, as popular with residents as with visitors.

F.n: OcciGabi Winery, Yoichi (オチガビワイナリー)
F.w: Founded in 2012 by the Ochii couple, who want to make Yoichi Japan's leading wine town. Tasting counter, terrace and a restaurant overlooking the vines.

F.n: Yoichi Winery (余市ワイナリー)
F.w: Makes its wine only from grapes grown and pressed in Yoichi, and runs a lunch restaurant on site.

F.n: NIKI Hills Winery, Niki (NIKI Hills Winery)
F.ad: Asahidai 148-1, Niki, Yoichi District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A hilltop winery with lodging above the Yoichi River valley, whose cool-climate wines have won international awards.

F.n: Otaru Milk Plant (小樽ミルクプラント)
F.w: Otaru's oldest soft-serve stand, run by Hoshō Gyūnyū in its 1936 milk-plant office.

F.n: Taishō Glass Kuboya, Sakaimachi (大正硝子 くぼ家)
F.w: A kissaten in the historic former Sakaiya shop on Sakaimachi Street, kept going by Taishō Glass.

F.n: Kita no Donburiya Takinami Shokudō, Sankaku Market (北のどんぶり屋 滝波食堂)
F.ad: Sankaku Market, Inaho 3-10-16, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The Takinami fish shop's diner in the Triangle Market — seafood from the tanks onto a pick-your-own bowl, with a queue every day.

F.n: New Sankō, Otaru (ニュー三幸)
F.ad: Sun Mall 1-bangai, Inaho 1-3-6, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A 1954 all-round restaurant, now known for its ankake yakisoba on house egg noodles. Bunkacho has named the dish a '100-Year Food'.

F.n: Otaru Ankake Yakisoba Kakuryū (小樽あんかけ焼きそば 鶴龍)
F.ad: Otaru Dejō Kōji, Ironai 1-1, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: An ankake-yakisoba specialist in the Dejō Kōji food alley by the canal.

F.n: Hakodate Wine Budōkan Honten (はこだてわいん 葡萄館本店)
F.ad: Kamifujishiro 11, Nanae, Kameda District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: One of Hokkaido's pioneer wineries (1973): about 80 wines on the shelves, a dozen to taste free, and a wine soft-serve sold only here.

F.n: Michi-no-eki YOU・Yū・Mori (道の駅 YOU・遊・もり)
F.ad: Kamidai-chō 326-18, Mori, Kayabe District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Route 5 roadside station of Mori, home of ikameshi — the squid-rice ekiben sold here in many forms, with Komagatake and Uchiura Bay from the roof lounge.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Kitamaebune Matsumae (道の駅 北前船 松前)
F.w: Clifftop roadside station on the Tsugaru Strait serving bowls of wild bluefin from the same waters as Ōma tuna, and Matsumae-zuke, the clan-era pickle of herring roe, kelp and squid.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Kaminokuni Monju (道の駅 上ノ国もんじゅ)
F.w: Sea-of-Japan roadside station whose restaurant window looks over the water; the signature is a tendon of local flounder.

F.n: Kamikawa Taisetsu Shuzō Ryokkyū-gura (上川大雪酒造 緑丘蔵)
F.ad: Asahi-machi 25-1, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: A 2017 regional-revival sake brewery at the foot of Daisetsuzan — pure sake only, from Hokkaido rice and mountain water.

F.n: Yakitori Senmon Ginneko (焼鳥専門 ぎんねこ)
F.w: The keeper of Asahikawa's soul food: a 1925 yakitori house in the Fura-Ri-To alley grilling a whole half chicken over charcoal in its never-emptied tare.

F.n: Taisetsu Ji-Beer-kan (大雪地ビール館)
F.w: A red-brick warehouse brewpub five minutes from Asahikawa Station pouring the local Taisetsu beers alongside fresh-lamb jingisukan.

F.n: Furano Wine Factory (ふらのワイン工場)
F.ad: Shimizuyama, Furano Budōgaoka Park, Furano, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The city-run brick winery on Shimizuyama hill (grapes since 1972): see the cellar and bottle-ageing rooms and taste factory-exclusive wines, free entry.

F.n: Furano Marché (フラノマルシェ)
F.w: Four buildings round a plaza near Furano Station: JA Furano's farm shop, a sweets bakery, ~2,000 local products and takeout stands cooking local ingredients.

F.n: Goshōteya Honpo, Esashi (五勝手屋本舗)
F.ad: Honchō 38, Esashi, Hiyama District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Esashi's 1870 confectioner, whose cylindrical azuki yōkan — sliced with the string on the tube — was presented to the Shōwa Emperor in 1936.

F.n: Kasshō Ryōri Ikasei Honten (活魚料理 いか清 本店)
F.w: Goryōkaku-side live-seafood house built around Hakodate's squid: the tank-fresh ma-ika is cut to order as glassy ikasōmen-style sashimi.

F.n: Yokoyama-ke, Esashi (横山家)
F.ad: Esashi Inishie Kaidō, Esashi, Hiyama District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: An old herring-merchant house on Esashi's Inishie Kaidō that serves the town's herring soba, topped with shredded nori.

F.n: Hakodate Goryō no Kura (函館五稜乃蔵)
F.ad: Kameo-chō (former Kameo school site), Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Kamikawa Taisetsu's 2021 Hakodate brewery — the city's first sake brewery in over half a century, with a Hakodate KOSEN lab inside and a shop; it shared top prize at a Hokkaido-rice sake competition.

F.n: Bräuhaus Ōnuma — Ōnuma Beer (ブロイハウス大沼)
F.ad: Ōnuma-chō 208, Nanae, Kameda District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The Ōnuma-park microbrewery: award-winning craft beers poured by the glass beside the lake station.

F.n: Shōga Rāmen Mizuno, Asahikawa (生姜ラーメン みづの)
F.w: Asahikawa's ginger-ramen original, invented by the founder in 1972 — a shōyu bowl sharpened with grated ginger.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Biei 'Oka no Kura' — Kōbaku Shokudō (道の駅 びえい「丘のくら」香麦食堂)
F.w: Stone-warehouse roadside station in central Biei whose dining room serves the town's curry udon both baked and as a dip, heaped with local vegetables.

F.n: Family Restaurant Daimaru, Biei (ファミリーレストラン だいまる)
F.w: Town diner whose curry udon is all-Biei: local wheat noodles, Biei vegetables and Biei pork.

F.n: Eki no Mieru Restaurant & Café KOERU, Biei (駅の見えるレストラン KOERU)
F.w: Station-view restaurant showcasing Biei wheat and the town's mochibuta pork — udon blended from several local wheat varieties.

F.n: Niseko Cheese Kōbō (ニセコチーズ工房)
F.ad: Kondō 425-6, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Small creamery making cheese from Niseko milk — World Cheese Awards 2021 super-gold for its long-aged 'Momiji' — with a café selling camembert soft-serve in summer.

F.n: Soba-dokoro Rakuichi (そば処 楽一)
F.ad: Niseko 431, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Soba master Tatsuru Rai's tiny counter (opened 2000) — the Niseko soba made famous by Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations; dinner is reservation-only.

F.n: Kamimura, Niseko (KAMIMURA)
F.ad: Hirafu, Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Niseko's fine-dining pioneer (2008): chef Yuichi Kamimura, trained under Tetsuya Wakuda in Sydney, holds a Michelin star from the Hokkaido guide.

F.n: Niseko Distillery (ニセコ蒸溜所)
F.ad: Niseko 478-15, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Opened 2021 beside Niseko's onsen area with Scottish pot stills and Annupuri spring water; its ohoro gin took the top gin award at the 2024 International Spirits Challenge.

F.n: Niseko Shuzō, Kutchan (二世古酒造)
F.ad: Asahi 47, Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Kutchan's century-old (1916) sake brewery at the foot of Yōtei, known for undiluted genshu; around 30 sakes to taste and buy, 15 minutes' walk from Kutchan Station.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Salmon Park Chitose (道の駅 サーモンパーク千歳)
F.w: Chitose's salmon-river roadside station beside the Chitose Aquarium and its Indian water-wheel — a six-stall food court built around salmon.

F.n: Umi no Eki Platto Minato Ichiba, Tomakomai (海の駅 ぷらっとみなと市場)
F.w: Tomakomai port's market hall — Japan's top hokki-clam catch sold fresh, eaten in hokki-don and hokki curry at the stalls, with a small hokki museum.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Date Rekishi no Mori (道の駅 だて歴史の杜)
F.w: Date's roadside station in its history park — Hansamu Shokudō, the scallop takikomi-gohan 'Date-musha' bento and Makiya's Date-milk pudding.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Tōya-ko (道の駅 とうや湖)
F.w: Hill-top roadside station above Lake Tōya with Mt Yōtei views; its shokudō and takeaway counter work the farm produce of the caldera rim.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Shiretoko-Rausu (道の駅 知床・らうす)
F.ad: Hon-chō, Rausu, Menashi District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The roadside station closest to Kunashir — its Shiretoko Shokudō is the local name for Rausu-landed hokke and kinki teishoku.

F.n: Kita no Kuni kara Jun no Banya, Rausu (北の国から 純の番屋)
F.ad: Funami-chō, Rausu, Menashi District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: The fishermen's hut from the drama 'Kita no Kuni kara 2002 Yuigon', rebuilt as a diner serving Rausu-coast seafood.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Swan 44 Nemuro (道の駅 スワン44ねむろ)
F.w: On Lake Fūren's swan shore — the Bird Pal dining room looks over the lagoon and is known for Nemuro's hanasaki-crab ramen.

F.n: Michi-no-eki Akan Tanchō no Sato (道の駅 阿寒丹頂の里)
F.w: Akan's crane-country roadside station (with an onsen) — Restaurant Tsuru grills local Ezo-shika venison.

F.n: Hanabatake Bokujō, Nakasatsunai (花畑牧場)
F.ad: Moto-Satsunai Higashi 4-sen 311-6, Nakasatsunai, Kasai District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Tanaka Yoshitaka's showcase ranch, birthplace of the nama-caramel boom — the café serves its own-cheese dishes and sweets.

F.n: Kamikawa Taisetsu Shuzō Hekiun-gura, Obihiro (上川大雪酒造 碧雲蔵)
F.ad: Obihiro University of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine campus, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Japan's first university-partnered sake brewery (2020), on the Obihiro agricultural university campus, brewing with Satsunai River water and Hokkaido rice.

F.n: Isoyakitei, Rishiri (磯焼亭)
F.ad: Oshidomari, Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
F.w: Opposite Oshidomari ferry terminal — Rishiri's raw bafun-uni bowls (Apr-Oct) and kombu-broth Rishiri ramen.

F.n: Kurumaya Genji, Wakkanai (車屋・源氏)
F.w: The Wakkanai name for takoshabu — paper-thin mizudako from the Sōya Strait swished in broth, the city's signature dish.

F.n: Karafuto Shokudō, Wakkanai (樺太食堂)
F.w: Seasonal fishermen-direct uni-don shack by Cape Noshappu, made famous by touring riders.
